summary: Target-level blueprint of the p-adic local Langlands correspondence for GL₂(ℚ_p). R30.1 fixes the conventions it rests on — GL₂(ℚ_p) and its mirabolic monoid P⁺, Colmez's dictionary between characters of ℚ_p^× and Galois characters (uniformisers ↦ geometric Frobenii, x|x| ↦ χ), the covariant Fontaine functor and the Tate dual imported from PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology, ψ and the treillis D^♮ ⊂ D^♯, the P(ℚ_p)-modules M ⊠ ℚ_p, rank-one modules R(δ) and trianguline representations, and the bridge from Colmez's LL(M) to the classical correspondence of GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R16.3. R30.2 specialises the smooth category of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups, the Banach duality of LocallyAnalyticDistributionsPartII ND.6 and locally analytic vectors to GL₂(ℚ_p), with Pontryagin duals, universal unitary completions, the mod p principal series and the Barthel–Livné–Breuil classification, the mod ℓ irreducibles of GL₂(ℤ_ℓ), U₀(ℓ), Ũ₀(ℓ) and what fails for F ≠ ℚ_p. R30.3 constructs D ⊠_δ ℙ¹, Colmez's Montreal functor D, V (and V̌), its values on irreducibles and Breuil's mod p correspondence, the contragredient, Π(D) and Π(V), Colmez's theorem V(Π(V)) = V, the Colmez–Dospinescu–Paškūnas bijection, Ext¹ injectivity and the locally analytic vectors of Π(D). R30.4 states LL(V) ⊗ Alg(V), Colmez's locally algebraic vectors theorem (with the supercuspidal case's global input recorded as gap G1), Berger–Breuil completions, Henniart's types, Kisin's Hypothesis (1.2.6), the classification of unitary completions (weights do not determine Π), Kirillov models, the trianguline locally analytic vectors and Dospinescu's de Rham extensions. R30.5 plans blocks and their classification with ρ̄_B, projective envelopes, the pseudodeformation ring of a block, Paškūnas's endomorphism-ring theorems, the Paškūnas–Tung local R = T, Kisin's deformation comparison, Nakamura's P̃ ≅ π*_{π̄} and Hom-removal, the Breuil–Mézard cycle identity, Paškūnas's support criterion, CDN's Kisin rings and BCDT admittance. R30.6 gives the case-by-case local theorems — Paškūnas (p ≥ 5), Hu–Tan, Tung (p odd and p = 2), Paškūnas at p = 2, Kisin's local inequality with Gee–Kisin's corrections, Paškūnas–Tung finiteness, block occurrence, Breuil–Strauch — and the hypothesis table consumed by modularity lifting.

nodes.title: The group GL₂(ℚ_p) and its standard subgroups
nodes.statement: Fix a prime p. Put G = GL₂(ℚ_p), K = GL₂(ℤ_p), Z ≅ ℚ_p^× the centre of scalar matrices, B the upper triangular Borel subgroup, T ⊂ B the diagonal torus, N ⊂ B the upper unipotent subgroup {(1 b; 0 1)}, and P the mirabolic subgroup {(a b; 0 1) : a ∈ ℚ_p^×, b ∈ ℚ_p} ≅ ℚ_p ⋊ ℚ_p^×. P(ℤ_p) = {(a b; 0 1) : a ∈ ℤ_p^×, b ∈ ℤ_p}, and P⁺ is the submonoid {(a b; 0 1) : a ∈ ℤ_p ∖ {0}, b ∈ ℤ_p} of P. Write w = (0 1; 1 0), φ_P = (p 0; 0 1), u = (1 1; 0 1) and σ_a = (a 0; 0 1) for a ∈ ℤ_p^×. KZ is the stabiliser of the vertex [ℤ_p²] of the Bruhat–Tits tree of PGL₂(ℚ_p), whose vertices are G/KZ; I₁ ⊂ K is the pro-p Iwahori subgroup of matrices congruent to (1 *; 0 1) mod p, I the Iwahori subgroup, and K₁ = ker(K → GL₂(𝔽_p)). These subgroups carry the topology induced from the p-adic topology of M₂(ℚ_p); K, P(ℤ_p), I and I₁ are compact open in their ambient groups.
hypotheses: p is a prime; all matrix groups are realised as units of 2×2 matrix rings over ℚ_p and ℤ_p (Mathlib's GL (Fin 2)).
proofSteps: Each subgroup is cut out of Mathlib's Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin 2) ℚ_[p] by conditions on the entries (zero lower-left entry for B, lower row (0,1) for P, entries in ℤ_p with unit determinant for K).
P⁺ is closed under multiplication because the product of (a b; 0 1) and (a' b'; 0 1) is (aa' ab'+b; 0 1), and a, a', b, b' ∈ ℤ_p with aa' ≠ 0.

G = BK (Iwasawa decomposition) and G = ⊔ K diag(p^a, p^b) K with a ≥ b (Cartan) are recorded from GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R16.1, which owns the rank-two Iwasawa and Cartan coordinates; they are cited, not planned again.
Colmez's convention identifies an étale (φ,Γ)-module with a P⁺-module: u acts as multiplication by 1+T, φ_P as φ and σ_a as the element of Γ with χ(σ_a) = a (Colmez, Introduction §4, Remark 0.4(iv)).
acceptance: w² = 1, w ∉ B, and wBw ∩ B = T.
P⁺ is a submonoid of P containing P(ℤ_p) and φ_P, and P(ℚ_p) is generated by P⁺ and φ_P⁻¹.
G = P·Z·K·{1, w} is not used; instead G is generated by P(ℚ_p), Z and w (Colmez, Introduction §4(iv): adding an action of w suffices to define an action of G).

nodes.title: Characters of ℚ_p^× as Galois characters (Colmez's normalisation)
nodes.statement: For a topological ring Λ let T̂(Λ) be the group of continuous characters δ : ℚ_p^× → Λ^×. Through local class field theory normalised so that p corresponds to a geometric Frobenius, W_{ℚ_p}^{ab} ≅ ℚ_p^×, and a character δ ∈ T̂(Λ) is viewed as the character of the Weil group W_{ℚ_p} given by δ(g) = δ(p)^{−deg g} · δ(χ(g)), where deg g ∈ ℤ is defined by g(x) = x^{p^{deg g}} on 𝔽̄_p and χ is the cyclotomic character. When n ↦ δ(p^n) extends continuously to ℤ̂ (in particular when Λ = k_L, or Λ = L and δ is unitary, i.e. v_p(δ(p)) = 0), δ extends to a continuous character of G_{ℚ_p}. Under this dictionary the character x ↦ x|x| corresponds to χ, its reduction ω mod p to the mod p cyclotomic character, and the unramified character μ_λ (μ_λ(p) = λ, trivial on ℤ_p^×) to the unramified character sending a geometric Frobenius to λ. For δ ∈ T̂(L) its weight is w(δ) = log δ(u)/log u for any u ∈ ℤ_p^× not a root of unity; for unitary δ it is the generalised Hodge–Tate weight of δ (w(x|x|) = 1).
hypotheses: L is a finite extension of ℚ_p with ring of integers O_L = O, uniformiser ϖ and residue field k_L = k.

The normalisation (uniformisers ↦ geometric Frobenii) is the one of Colmez, Paškūnas and Colmez–Dospinescu–Paškūnas; GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R16.3 uses the same Art_F(ϖ) = geometric Frobenius, and PadicHodgeTheory R06.2 states crystalline characters through Art^arith, the inverse normalisation.
proofSteps: Local class field theory for ℚ_p: the reciprocity isomorphism ℚ_p^× ≅ W_{ℚ_p}^{ab} with p ↦ geometric Frobenius (trivial on μ_{p^∞}) and u ∈ ℤ_p^× ↦ the element acting on μ_{p^∞} by u, so that the inverse map is g ↦ p^{−deg g} χ(g) (cited from the Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory roadmap through GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R16.3, which fixes Art_F).
Compute x|x| on p^{−deg g}χ(g): |p^{−deg g}χ(g)| = p^{deg g}, so (x|x|)(p^{−deg g}χ(g)) = χ(g); hence x|x| ↔ χ, and reducing mod ϖ gives ω.

δ extends from W_{ℚ_p} = ℤ-extension to G_{ℚ_p} = ℤ̂-extension exactly when n ↦ δ(p)^n extends continuously to ℤ̂, which holds when δ(p) is a unit of a profinite or p-adically complete-with-unit-group-containing-it ring (k_L^×, O_L^×).
The weight is well defined because δ restricted to a small open subgroup 1 + p^nℤ_p is u ↦ exp(w(δ) log u) (Colmez, Représentations triangulines, §0.1).
acceptance: x|x| ↦ χ and ω ↦ the mod p cyclotomic character; the unramified μ_λ ↦ the unramified character with geometric Frobenius ↦ λ.
For two characters, δ₁δ₂ ↦ (δ₁)(δ₂): the dictionary is a group isomorphism onto the continuous characters of W_{ℚ_p}.
The character x ↦ x of ℚ_p^× (weight 1, δ(p) = p) does not extend to G_{ℚ_p}, since n ↦ p^n has no continuous extension to ℤ̂.

nodes.title: Étale (φ,Γ)-modules over O_E, E, E† and R with the covariant Fontaine functor
nodes.statement: Let O_E be the ring of Laurent series Σ_{k∈ℤ} a_k T^k with a_k ∈ O_L and a_k → 0 as k → −∞, E = O_E[1/p], O_E⁺ = O_L[[T]], E† ⊂ E the overconvergent subfield and R the Robba ring over L, with the commuting actions φ(T) = (1+T)^p − 1 and σ_a(T) = (1+T)^a − 1 (a ∈ ℤ_p^× ≅ Γ). The categories in use are ΦΓ^et_tors (étale (φ,Γ)-modules of finite length over O_E), ΦΓ^et(O_E), ΦΓ^et(E), ΦΓ^et(E†) and ΦΓ^et(R) (slope 0, free of finite rank). The covariant Fontaine functors are D(V) = (A ⊗_{ℤ_p} V)^H and V(D) = ((O_L·A) ⊗_{O_E} D)^{φ=1}, with A the p-adic completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_{ℚ_p} and H = ker χ; they are exact quasi-inverse equivalences Rep_tors G_{ℚ_p} ≅ ΦΓ^et_tors, Rep_{O_L} G_{ℚ_p} ≅ ΦΓ^et(O_E) and Rep_L G_{ℚ_p} ≅ ΦΓ^et(E) ≅ ΦΓ^et(E†) ≅ ΦΓ^et(R) (D ↦ D† ↦ D_rig = R ⊗ D†). The Tate dual of a representation is V̌ = Hom(V, L ⊗ χ) (resp. Hom(V, O_L ⊗ χ), Hom(V, L/O_L ⊗ χ)), and V(Ď) = V̌ for the Tate dual Ď of R30.1/tate-dual. This node fixes these conventions for the whole roadmap; the rings, the equivalences and the overconvergence theorem are owned by PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology PG.0–PG.2 and PadicHodgeTheory P7:annulus-foundations and are not constructed here.
hypotheses: p any prime; L/ℚ_p finite.
The overconvergence and Robba-ring steps are imported with their fixed-field hypotheses (PG.2) and Kedlaya's slope theory behind ΦΓ^et(E†) ≅ ΦΓ^et(R).
proofSteps: PG.0 supplies O_E, E, the commuting φ and Γ actions and the étale lattice interface; PG.1 Fontaine's equivalence in its integral, torsion and rational forms; PG.2 the Cherbonnier–Colmez overconvergence and the Robba realisation; PadicHodgeTheory P7:annulus-foundations/robba-ring the Robba ring itself and P7/robba-realisation-comparison the realisation D_rig.

Colmez's Théorème I.3.1 states the equivalences with exactly the covariant functors above; this node records that choice so that R30.3's V(Π) (Tate dual of V(D(Π))) and Π(D) (with D(Π(D)) = Ď) have their stated variance.
Exactness and compatibility with Tate duals are part of the imported equivalence; V(Ď) = V̌ follows from the pairing D × Ď → O_E dT/(1+T) (R30.1/tate-dual).
acceptance: For V = O_L (trivial), D(V) = O_E.
For V = O_L(χ), D(V) = O_E ⊗ e with φ(e) = e and σ_a(e) = a e.
D(V ⊗ W) = D(V) ⊗ D(W) and D is exact.

nodes.title: The Tate dual of an étale (φ,Γ)-module and the rank-two twist
nodes.statement: For D ∈ ΦΓ^et(O_E) (resp. ΦΓ^et(E), ΦΓ^et_tors) the Tate dual is Ď = Hom_{O_E}(D, O_E dT/(1+T)) (resp. with E dT/(1+T), (E/O_E) dT/(1+T)) with the induced φ and Γ, where dT/(1+T) carries φ(dT/(1+T)) = dT/(1+T) and σ_a(dT/(1+T)) = a dT/(1+T); the residue of the pairing gives a perfect pairing { , } : Ď × D → O_L, and V(Ď) = V̌. If D has rank 2, then ∧²D = E ⊗ α_D for the character α_D ∈ T̂(O_L) attached to det V(D) by R30.1/character-dictionary, δ_D := (x|x|)^{−1}α_D, and x ↦ x ⊗ δ_D^{−1} is an isomorphism D ≅ Ď ⊗ δ_D, i.e. Ď ≅ D ⊗ δ_D^{−1}.
hypotheses: D étale over O_E or E; for the rank-two identity, D of rank 2.
proofSteps: The residue map res₀ : O_E dT → O_L gives the pairing {x, y} = res₀(⟨σ_{−1}x, y⟩) used by Colmez; perfectness follows from the perfectness of the residue pairing on O_E.
For rank 2 the wedge pairing D × D → ∧²D = E ⊗ α_D is perfect; twisting by the character of dT/(1+T), which is that of x|x| (χ), identifies D with Hom(D, E ⊗ α_D) ⊗ ... and gives Ď ≅ D ⊗ δ_D^{−1}.
V(Ď) = V̌ follows from Fontaine's equivalence applied to the pairing (R30.1/fontaine-functor-convention).
acceptance: For D = O_E (trivial), Ď = O_E ⊗ (x|x|), i.e. V(Ď) = O_L(χ).
For D of rank 2 with det V(D) = χ (α_D = x|x|), δ_D = 1 and Ď ≅ D.

nodes.title: The operator ψ and the lattices D⁺, D^♮ and D^♯
nodes.statement: Let D be an étale (φ,Γ)-module over O_E (torsion or free). Every x ∈ D is uniquely Σ_{i=0}^{p−1} (1+T)^i φ(x_i), and ψ(x) := x₀ is the left inverse of φ commuting with Γ (PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology PG.4). Define D⁺ = {z : (φ^n(z))_n bounded}, D⁺⁺ = {z : φ^n(z) → 0}, D^{nr} = ∩_n φ^n(D), D^♮ = the smallest compact O_E⁺-submodule of D that is stable under ψ and generates D, and D^♯ = the largest compact O_E⁺-submodule of D stable under ψ on which ψ is surjective; for D ∈ ΦΓ^et(E) these are L·Δ^♮, L·Δ^♯ etc. for a φ- and Γ-stable O_E-lattice Δ. Then D⁺⁺ ⊂ D⁺ ⊂ D^♮ ⊂ D^♯, D⁺ = D^{nr} ⊕ D⁺⁺, a surjection D → D₁ of étale modules induces surjections D^♮ → D₁^♮ and D^♯ → D₁^♯, D^{nr} = 0 when V(D)^{H'} = 0 (e.g. D irreducible of rank ≥ 2), and for D torsion, in the residue pairing Ď × D → O_L the orthogonal of D^♮ is Ď⁺ and that of D^♯ is Ď⁺⁺, so D^♯/D^♮ is dual to Ď^{nr}.
hypotheses: D étale over O_E; the existence of D^♮ and D^♯ is Colmez's (from his Iwasawa-theory paper [35]).
proofSteps: ψ is imported from PG.4/linearized-psi with its uniqueness and Γ-compatibility.

Existence of D^♮, D^♯ and the inclusions D⁺⁺ ⊂ D⁺ ⊂ D^♮ ⊂ D^♯ are recalled in Colmez §I.3.2 from his earlier paper ([35, II.4–II.5]); they are planned here as recalled statements with that proof route.

Surjectivity under quotients (Proposition I.3.2), the description of D^{nr} (Proposition I.3.3) and the duality (Proposition I.3.4) follow from the finite-length theory for torsion modules and passage to the limit.
acceptance: Example: for D = E (trivial), D⁺ = D^♮ = E⁺, D⁺⁺ = T E⁺, D^{nr} = L and D^♯ = T^{−1}E⁺ (Colmez p. 33).
D ↦ D^♮ and D ↦ D^♯ are not exact (Colmez §VII.4.7 shows D ↦ D^♮ ⊠ P¹ is not exact).

sources.locator: §I.3.2, pp. 33–35: the definitions, Example, Propositions I.3.2–I.3.4
sources.match: Defines D⁺⁺, D⁺, D^{nr}, D^♮ and D^♯, computes them for D = E, records D⁺⁺ ⊂ D⁺ ⊂ D^♮ ⊂ D^♯ and D⁺ = D^{nr} ⊕ D⁺⁺, surjectivity on D^♮ and D^♯ under quotient maps, the description of D^{nr} and the orthogonality statements.

nodes.title: (P(ℤ_p),ψ)-modules and the P(ℚ_p)-module M ⊠ ℚ_p
nodes.statement: A (P(ℤ_p),ψ)-module is an O_L-module M with an action of P(ℤ_p) and an O_L-linear ψ commuting with (ℤ_p^× 0; 0 1) and satisfying ψ((1 pb; 0 1)z) = (1 b; 0 1)ψ(z). An étale (φ,Γ)-module is one through the dictionary of R30.1/gl2qp-subgroups and ψ of R30.1/psi-and-treillis; so are D^♮ and D^♯. For such M, M ⊠ ℚ_p is the module of sequences (x^{(n)})_{n∈ℕ} in M with ψ(x^{(n+1)}) = x^{(n)}, and there is a unique action of P(ℚ_p) on M ⊠ ℚ_p with (a 0; 0 1)·(x^{(n)}) = ((a 0; 0 1)x^{(n)}) for a ∈ ℤ_p^×, (p^k 0; 0 1)·(x^{(n)}) = (x^{(n+k)}) and (1 b; 0 1)·(x^{(n)}) = ((1 p^n b; 0 1)x^{(n)})_{n ≥ −v_p(b)}. For M the O_L-valued measures D⁰(ℤ_p, O_L) (with ψ = (p^{−1} 0; 0 1) ∘ Res_{pℤ_p}), M ⊠ ℚ_p = D⁰(ℚ_p, O_L) with (a b; 0 1) acting by x ↦ ax + b. Restrictions Res_U : D ⊠ ℚ_p → D ⊠ U to compact opens U ⊂ ℚ_p are defined, D ⊠ ℤ_p = D and D ⊠ ℤ_p^× = D^{ψ=0}; adjoining the action of the centre (d 0; 0 d) by δ(d) gives the B-module D ⊠_δ ℚ_p.

proofSteps: Uniqueness: the three formulas determine the action on the generators of P(ℚ_p) (R30.1/gl2qp-subgroups); existence is checked on relations, using that ψ commutes with (ℤ_p^× 0; 0 1) and the twisted commutation with unipotents (Colmez Proposition 0.5).
For measures, (x^{(n)}) ↦ the measure on ℚ_p whose restriction to p^{−n}ℤ_p is x^{(n)} rescaled identifies the inverse limit with D⁰(ℚ_p, O_L).
D ⊠ ℤ_p^× = D^{ψ=0} follows from the decomposition D = φ(D) ⊕ D^{ψ=0} (PG.4/psi-zero-splitting).
acceptance: For D⁰(ℤ_p, O_L): M ⊠ ℚ_p = D⁰(ℚ_p, O_L) with the affine action.
Res_{ℤ_p}∘(p^k 0; 0 1) recovers x^{(k)}.

nodes.title: Rank-one (φ,Γ)-modules R(δ) over the Robba ring
nodes.statement: For δ ∈ T̂(L), R(δ) is the (φ,Γ)-module over the Robba ring R = R_L that is R itself with φ multiplied by δ(p) and γ ∈ Γ multiplied by δ(χ(γ)). (i) Every (φ,Γ)-module of rank 1 over R is isomorphic to R(δ) for a unique δ ∈ T̂(L). (ii) R(δ) has Kedlaya slope v_p(δ(p)); it is étale (slope 0) iff δ is unitary, and then R(δ) = D_rig(δ) for δ viewed as a Galois character. (iii) Ext¹(R(δ₂), R(δ₁)) = Ext¹(R, R(δ₁δ₂^{−1})) = H¹(δ₁δ₂^{−1}) is one-dimensional over L unless δ₁δ₂^{−1} is x^{−i} (i ∈ ℕ) or |x|x^i (i ≥ 1), when it is two-dimensional, with projectivisation ℙ¹(L).
hypotheses: p ≠ 2 in the source read (Colmez, Représentations triangulines, §0.1 and its footnote 1); the p = 2 case of (i) and (iii) is recorded as gap G2 of this packet.
L/ℚ_p finite; R = R_L the Robba ring over L.
proofSteps: (i): a rank-one module is R·e with φ(e) = a e and γ(e) = b(γ) e; Colmez's Proposition 3.1 shows that after changing e one may take a ∈ L^× and b a character of Γ with values in L^×, and δ is recovered by δ(p) = a, δ|_{ℤ_p^×} = b∘χ^{−1}.
(ii): Kedlaya's slope filtration (PG.2 / PadicHodgeTheory P7) gives the slope v_p(δ(p)); étaleness iff slope 0.
(iii): Colmez's computation of H⁰, H¹ of R(δ) via the Herr complex (PG.3) and the operator ∂ = (1+T)d/dT (Théorème 2.9 there).
acceptance: R(x|x|) = D_rig(χ).
R(1) = R and R(x^{−i}) has H⁰ ≠ 0 (contains t^i).
dim H¹(1) = 2 = dim Hom(ℚ_p^×, L).

nodes.title: Trianguline representations of dimension 2 and Colmez's parameter space
nodes.statement: A two-dimensional L-representation V of G_{ℚ_p} is trianguline if D_rig(V) is an extension 0 → R(δ₁) → D_rig(V) → R(δ₂) → 0 (R30.1/rank-one-robba-modules). Colmez's space S parametrises s = (δ₁, δ₂, ℒ) with ℒ ∈ ℙ(Ext¹(R(δ₂), R(δ₁))) (a point except on the loci δ₁δ₂^{−1} = x^i|x| (i ≥ 1) or x^{−i} (i ≥ 0), where it is ℙ¹(L)); S₊ is cut out by v_p(δ₁(p)) + v_p(δ₂(p)) = 0 and v_p(δ₁(p)) ≥ 0, with u(s) = v_p(δ₁(p)), w(s) = w(δ₁) − w(δ₂), and S₊ = S^{ng} ⊔ S^{cris} ⊔ S^{st} ⊔ S^{ord} ⊔ S^{ncl}, S_irr = S^{ng}_* ⊔ S^{cris}_* ⊔ S^{st}_* (∗: u(s) > 0). For s ∈ S_* ∖ S^{ncl}_*, D(s) is étale and V(s) := V(D(s)) is trianguline; V(s) is irreducible iff s ∈ S_irr; det V(s) = δ₁δ₂ and its Hodge–Tate weights are w(δ₁), w(δ₂); every irreducible trianguline V is some V(s), and V(s) ≅ V(s') for s ≠ s' in S_irr iff s, s' ∈ S^{cris}_* and s' = (x^{w(s)}δ₂, x^{−w(s)}δ₁, ∞). A two-dimensional crystalline V is trianguline iff the φ-eigenvalues on D_cris(V) lie in L; every two-dimensional semistable V is trianguline.
hypotheses: p ≠ 2 in the source read (Colmez, Représentations triangulines, §0.1, footnote 1); the p = 2 case is gap G2.

proofSteps: The parameter space and its stratification are defined from the rank-one classification and the Ext¹ computation (R30.1/rank-one-robba-modules).
Slope 0 of D(s) for s ∈ S_* ∖ S^{ncl}_* and irreducibility for s ∈ S_irr: Colmez's Théorème 0.5, via Kedlaya's slope filtration.
Hodge–Tate weights and determinant: Colmez's Propositions 4.4–4.5, via Sen theory on D_dif (PadicHodgeTheory P7/fontaine-dif-module).
Crystalline and semistable criteria: Théorème 0.8 and Remarque 0.9, using Berger's dictionary D_cris, D_st from D_rig (PadicHodgeTheory P7/berger-dcris-dst-dictionary).

nodes.title: Colmez's classical correspondence LL(M) against R16.3
nodes.statement: Let M be a two-dimensional representation of the Weil–Deligne group WD_{ℚ_p} over L that is not a twist of the trivial representation by a character, with Frobenius normalised as in PadicHodgeTheory R06.3/weil-deligne-parameter and characters read through R30.1/character-dictionary. Colmez's LL(M) is: Ind_B^G(δ₁ ⊗ δ₂|·|^{−1}) (≅ Ind_B^G(δ₂ ⊗ δ₁|·|^{−1})) for M = δ₁ ⊕ δ₂ with δ₁ ∉ {δ₂, δ₂|·|, δ₂|·|^{−1}}; for M = δ ⊕ δ|·| with N = 0, the reducible Ind_B^G(δ|·| ⊗ δ|·|^{−1}), an extension of δ∘det by St ⊗ (δ∘det); for M = δ ⊕ δ|·| with N ≠ 0, St ⊗ (δ∘det); for the non-split extension of δ by δ, Ind_B^G(δ ⊗ δ|·|^{−1}); and for M irreducible, the supercuspidal rec^{−1}(M). For a filtration with jumps a < b put LL(M, Fil) = LL(M) ⊗ W_{a,b−a} with W_{a,k} = Sym^{k−1} ⊗ det^a. The bridge theorem: for M not of the form δ ⊕ δ|·| with N = 0, LL(M) is the irreducible π with rec(π) ⊗ ν^{1/2} ≅ M, where rec is the unitary correspondence of GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R16.3 and ν = |·|; equivalently M ≅ recᵀ(π) ⊗ ν for the Tate normalisation recᵀ(π) = rec(π) ⊗ ν^{−1/2} of R16.3/tate-unitary-normalization, so det M = ω_π·ν. In the case M = δ ⊕ δ|·| with N = 0, Colmez takes the full reducible principal series Ind_B^G(δ|·| ⊗ δ|·|^{−1}) instead of the one-dimensional Langlands quotient that rec^{−1} attaches. Colmez’s functor V and the Kisin–Emerton functor MF differ by a Tate twist: V(π) = MF(π)(ε).
hypotheses: M two-dimensional, not a character twist of the trivial representation.
The geometric-Frobenius normalisation on both sides (R30.1/character-dictionary, R16.3).
proofSteps: Write each case of Colmez's list in R16.3's normalised induction i_B^G(a, b) = Ind_B^G(a|·|^{1/2} ⊗ b|·|^{−1/2}): Ind_B^G(δ₁ ⊗ δ₂|·|^{−1}) = i_B^G(δ₁|·|^{−1/2}, δ₂|·|^{−1/2}), whose unitary parameter is (δ₁ ⊕ δ₂)|·|^{−1/2} by R16.3/principal-series-parameter; twisting by ν^{1/2} gives M, and R16.3/tate-unitary-normalization rewrites this as recᵀ ⊗ ν.
The Steinberg case: R16.3/steinberg-monodromy gives the monodromy-nonzero parameter of St ⊗ (δ∘det), matching Colmez's N ≠ 0 case.
The N = 0 non-generic case is where Colmez's LL differs from rec^{−1}: R16.3 attaches the one-dimensional Langlands quotient, Colmez the reducible principal series; record the difference explicitly.
Supercuspidal case: R16.3/supercuspidal-parameter with the same twist by ν^{1/2}.
V(π) = MF(π)(ε): Colmez defines V(Π) as the Tate dual of V(D(Π)), Emerton defines MF(π) as its Pontryagin dual (Emerton lg §3.2, footnote 6), and the two duals differ by χ.
acceptance: For M = μ_α ⊕ μ_β unramified with α/β ∉ {1, p, p^{−1}}, LL(M) = Ind_B^G(μ_α ⊗ μ_β|·|^{−1}) has central character μ_{αβ}|·|^{−1}, and its unitary parameter under R16.3 is (μ_α ⊕ μ_β)|·|^{−1/2}.
For M = δ ⊕ δ|·| with N ≠ 0, LL(M) = St ⊗ (δ∘det), whose R16.3 parameter δ|·|^{1/2} ⊕ δ|·|^{−1/2} with nonzero monodromy becomes M after the twist by |·|^{1/2}.
LL(M ⊗ η) = LL(M) ⊗ (η∘det) for a character η, and the central character of LL(M) is det(M)·|·|^{−1}.

nodes.title: Smooth, locally finite and locally admissible torsion representations of GL₂(ℚ_p)
nodes.statement: Let ζ : Z → O^× be a continuous character. Mod^{sm}_{G}(O) is the category of smooth representations of G = GL₂(ℚ_p) on O-torsion modules (every vector has open stabiliser; the module carries the discrete topology), and Mod^{sm}_{G,ζ}(O) its full subcategory on which Z acts through ζ. A smooth π is admissible if π^H[ϖ^n] is a finitely generated O-module for every compact open H and n; locally admissible if O[G]v is admissible for every v; locally finite if O[G]v has finite length for every v. Mod^{l.adm}_{G,ζ}(O) ⊂ Mod^{sm}_{G,ζ}(O) and Mod^{l.fin}_{G,ζ}(O) are the corresponding full subcategories, and Rep^{tors}G (Colmez) is the category of smooth admissible O_L[G]-modules of finite length with a central character; Rep^{ℓf}G is the category of finite length smooth objects. These specialise the smooth category of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.0 (coefficients A = O/ϖ^n, G = GL₂(ℚ_p)); they are abelian, closed under subquotients and arbitrary direct sums (for l.adm and l.fin), and are Grothendieck categories in which every object has an injective envelope. For G = GL₂(ℚ_p) every irreducible smooth representation is admissible and finitely presented, so Rep^{ℓf}G ⊂ Rep^{adm}G ∩ Rep^{pf}G and the finite length objects of Mod^{l.adm}_{G,ζ}(O) and Mod^{l.fin}_{G,ζ}(O) coincide with Rep^{tors}G.
hypotheses: O = O_L, ϖ, k = k_L as in R30.1/character-dictionary; ζ continuous.
The finite-length statement uses the classification of R30.2/modp-irreducibles, which is special to F = ℚ_p.
proofSteps: Import the smooth category over a ring, admissibility and local admissibility from SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.0 (SR.0.1–SR.0.4 and SR.0:derived-extension.1, which proves the Grothendieck property and supplies injective envelopes) and specialise to A = O/ϖ^n and G = GL₂(ℚ_p).
Smoothness at the pin is Tau Ceti's IsSmoothDiscrete on TopRep (discrete module, open point stabilisers).

Every irreducible smooth representation is admissible and finitely presented (CDN 2023 §1.2.3, from Barthel–Livné and Breuil), and both properties are stable under extensions, giving Rep^{ℓf}G ⊂ Rep^{adm}G ∩ Rep^{pf}G; hence a locally finite object is locally admissible and finite length objects are admissible.

Locally admissible ⇒ locally finite: O[G]v is finitely generated and admissible, hence has admissible cosocle, hence finite length (CDN 2023 Théorème 1.21 for objects killed by ϖ, and dévissage along ϖ-adic filtrations).
Gabriel's theory of locally finite Grothendieck categories applies (Paškūnas 2013 §2 and [35, §IV] there).
acceptance: The trivial representation and Ind_B^G(χ₁ ⊗ χ₂) lie in Mod^{l.fin}_{G,ζ}(k) for the matching ζ.
c-Ind_{KZ}^G σ is smooth but not locally finite: it is a free k[T]-module of infinite rank (FiniteFlat R07.5).

nodes.title: The Pontryagin dual category C_{G,ζ}(O) of compact O[[K]]-modules
nodes.statement: Fix a compact open H ⊂ G (one may take H = K or I₁). Mod^{pro aug}_G(O) is Emerton's category of profinite O[[H]]-modules with an O[G]-action that agrees with the O[[H]]-action on O[H]; π ↦ π^∨ = Hom^{cont}_O(π, L/O) is an anti-equivalence Mod^{sm}_G(O) ≅ Mod^{pro aug}_G(O). C_{G,ζ}(O) is the full subcategory anti-equivalent to Mod^{l.adm}_{G,ζ}(O) (or to Mod^{l.fin}_{G,ζ}(O)), C_{G,ζ}(k) the objects killed by ϖ. Since anti-equivalences reverse arrows, every object of C_{G,ζ}(O) has a projective envelope; an object M of C(O) is admissible iff M is a finitely generated O[[H]]-module (equivalently M^∨ is admissible), and O[[H]] is the completed group algebra of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1.
hypotheses: H compact open in G; O[[H]] = lim O/ϖ^n[H/H'] over open normal H'.
proofSteps: Pontryagin duality for discrete torsion O-modules versus compact O-modules (Mathlib PontryaginDual over the circle, specialised to L/O) gives the anti-equivalence on underlying modules; the G-action is transported and is compatible with the O[[H]]-module structure by smoothness.

Admissibility ⇔ finite generation over O[[H]]: π^{H'}[ϖ] finite for all H' ⇔ π^∨/𝔪 finite-dimensional ⇔ π^∨ finitely generated by topological Nakayama (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L5, compact inverse systems and topological Nakayama).
Projective envelopes in C(O) are duals of injective envelopes in Mod^{l.adm}_{G,ζ}(O) (R30.2/smooth-torsion-categories).
acceptance: The dual of the trivial representation k is k.
(c-Ind_{KZ}^G σ)^∨ is not finitely generated over O[[K]], matching non-admissibility.

nodes.title: Admissible unitary Banach representations of GL₂(ℚ_p)
nodes.statement: A unitary L-Banach representation Π of G is an L-Banach space with a continuous G-action admitting an open bounded G-stable O-lattice Θ; Π is admissible if Θ/ϖΘ is an admissible smooth k-representation (equivalently Θ^d = Hom^{cont}_O(Θ, O) is finitely generated over O[[K]], equivalently Π restricted to one, hence every, compact open subgroup is admissible in the sense of Schneider–Teitelbaum). Ban^{adm}_{G,ζ}(L) is the category of admissible unitary L-Banach representations with central character ζ; it is abelian, being anti-equivalent through Θ ↦ Θ^d ⊗ L to finitely generated L ⊗ O[[K]]-modules with compatible G-action. Π is residually of finite length if Θ/ϖΘ has finite length (independent of Θ, with Π̄^{ss} := (Θ/ϖΘ)^{ss} independent of Θ); Rep_L G (Colmez, CDP) is the full subcategory of Π with a central character and residually of finite length, Rep_{O_L}G the p-adically complete separated ϖ-torsion-free O[G]-modules Θ with Θ/ϖ^nΘ ∈ Rep^{tors}G. An absolutely irreducible Π is ordinary if it is a subquotient of a unitary parabolic induction (Ind_B^G η₁ ⊗ η₂)^{cont} of unitary characters.
hypotheses: Coefficients L/ℚ_p finite; Π with central character for Ban^{adm}_{G,ζ}(L).
proofSteps: Specialise LocallyAnalyticDistributionsPartII ND.6/banach-iwasawa-duality (Schneider–Teitelbaum Lemma 3.4 and Theorem 3.5 for the compact group K) and transport the G-action; independence of the compact open subgroup is the requested compact-open test (request to LocallyAnalyticDistributionsPartII ND.6).
Θ/ϖΘ admissible ⇔ Θ^d/ϖ finitely generated over k[[K]] ⇔ Θ^d finitely generated over O[[K]] (topological Nakayama, R30.2/pontryagin-dual-category).
Residual finite length and the independence of Π̄^{ss} from Θ: any two open bounded lattices are commensurable, and semisimplification of Θ/ϖ is a Brauer–Nesbitt type invariant (CDP §1.1).
By CDP Corollary 1.6, an object of Ban^{adm}_G(L) has finite length iff it is residually of finite length (R30.3/cdp-correspondence).
acceptance: The universal unitary completion of the smooth Steinberg is in Ban^{adm}_{G,1}(L).
(Ind_B^G η₁ ⊗ η₂)^{cont} for unitary η_i is admissible, residually of finite length and ordinary.
A representation with non-unitary central character is never unitary.

nodes.title: Locally analytic and locally algebraic vectors of GL₂(ℚ_p)-representations
nodes.statement: For Π ∈ Ban^{adm}_G(L), v ∈ Π is locally analytic if g ↦ gv is a locally analytic function G → Π, and locally algebraic if g ↦ gv is locally a polynomial in a, b, c, d and (ad − bc)^{−1} with coefficients in Π. Π^{an} and Π^{alg} ⊂ Π^{an} are G-stable; Π^{an} is an admissible locally analytic representation, dense in Π, and Π ↦ Π^{an} is exact on Ban^{adm}_G(L) (Schneider–Teitelbaum), while Π^{alg} is zero in general. Π^{alg} = ⊕_W W ⊗ Hom_{𝔤}(W, Π)^{sm} over irreducible algebraic representations W = Sym^{k−1}L² ⊗ det^a (k ≥ 1, a ∈ ℤ); a representation is of type (ℓ, k) if only W_{ℓ,k} := Sym^{k−1} ⊗ det^ℓ occurs. Admissible locally analytic representations are the strong duals of coadmissible D(H, L)-modules for compact open H, with D(H, L) the Fréchet–Stein distribution algebra of LocallyAnalyticDistributionsPartII ND.1–ND.2.
hypotheses: Π admissible unitary Banach; G = GL₂(ℚ_p) viewed as a locally ℚ_p-analytic group.
proofSteps: Specialise the general theory of admissible locally analytic representations and of the functor Π ↦ Π^{an} (Schneider–Teitelbaum, requested from LocallyAnalyticDistributionsPartII ND.2) to G.
Density and exactness of Π ↦ Π^{an}: from Fréchet–Stein flatness of D(H, L) over L ⊗ O[[H]] (ND.2/faithful-flatness) applied to the finitely generated dual of Π.

Decomposition of Π^{alg}: an algebraic vector generates a finite-dimensional 𝔤-module, decomposed into irreducible algebraic representations; the multiplicity spaces are smooth (Colmez Proposition VI.2.4).
acceptance: For Π = W finite-dimensional algebraic and unitary (only when W is a character), Π^{alg} = Π.
Π^{alg} ⊂ Π^{an} ⊂ Π.
For a unitary principal series (Ind_B^G δ₁ ⊗ δ₂)^{cont} with δ₁δ₂^{−1} not locally algebraic, Π^{alg} = 0.

nodes.title: Universal unitary completions
nodes.statement: Let W be a locally convex L-representation of G (for instance a locally algebraic representation π ⊗ W or Π^{an}). A universal unitary completion of W is a unitary L-Banach representation Ŵ with a continuous G-map ι : W → Ŵ such that every continuous G-map W → B into a unitary Banach representation B factors uniquely through ι. It exists iff W has a G-stable separated O-lattice that is finitely generated over O[G] after restricting to any finitely generated O[G]-submodule (Emerton's criterion); when W = π ⊗ W_alg is locally algebraic with π finitely generated and Θ a finitely generated G-stable lattice, Ŵ = L ⊗ (lim Θ/ϖ^nΘ) modulo ϖ-divisible elements. Colmez–Dospinescu: for Π ∈ Rep_L(G), Π is the universal unitary completion of Π^{an}.
hypotheses: W locally convex with continuous G-action; for the existence statement a finitely generated G-stable lattice.
proofSteps: Construct Ŵ as the Hausdorff completion of W for the gauge of a finitely generated G-stable lattice; the universal property follows because any continuous G-map to a unitary B sends a finitely generated lattice into a bounded set.
Uniqueness up to unique isomorphism from the universal property.

Colmez–Dospinescu Théorème 0.2: for Π ∈ Rep_L(G) the restriction Hom_G(Π, B) → Hom_G(Π^{an}, B) is bijective for every unitary Banach B; their proof uses coherence of Π (Théorème 0.7) and the description of Π(D)^{an} (R30.3/analytic-vectors-of-pi).
acceptance: The universal completion of the trivial representation is L.
For Π ∈ Rep_L(G), (Π^{an})^ ≅ Π (Colmez–Dospinescu).

nodes.title: Mod p principal series and Steinberg representations
nodes.statement: For smooth characters δ₁, δ₂ : ℚ_p^× → k^× write δ₁ ⊗ δ₂ for the character (a b; 0 d) ↦ δ₁(a)δ₂(d) of B and Ind_B^G for smooth induction (locally constant φ : G → k with φ(bg) = (δ₁ ⊗ δ₂)(b)φ(g), G acting by right translation). Colmez's normalisation is B(δ₁, δ₂) := Ind_B^G(δ₂ ⊗ δ₁ω^{−1}), an object of Rep^{tors}G with central character ω^{−1}δ₁δ₂, irreducible unless δ₁ = ωδ, δ₂ = δ for some δ, in which case it is a non-split extension of St ⊗ (δ∘det) by δ∘det, St being the Steinberg representation Ind_B^G(1)/1. Paškūnas and CDP use π{χ₁, χ₂} := (Ind_B^G χ₁ ⊗ χ₂ω^{−1})^{ss} ⊕ (Ind_B^G χ₂ ⊗ χ₁ω^{−1})^{ss}, of length 2 in general, 3 or 4 for the exceptional pairs, and CDN write I(χ₁, χ₂) for the irreducible principal series attached to (χ₁, χ₂).
hypotheses: δ₁, δ₂ smooth characters with values in k^× (after enlarging k).
proofSteps: Barthel–Livné: Ind_B^G(χ₁ ⊗ χ₂) is irreducible iff χ₁ ≠ χ₂, and Ind_B^G(χ ⊗ χ) is a non-split extension of St ⊗ χ by χ∘det (FiniteFlat R07.5 and Colmez Proposition III.3.7).
The central character of Ind_B^G(δ₂ ⊗ δ₁ω^{−1}) is δ₂·δ₁ω^{−1} restricted to scalars.
Intertwinings between Jordan–Hölder constituents of different principal series do not occur unless the parameters agree (Colmez Proposition III.3.5(ii)).
acceptance: B(δ₁, δ₂) has central character ω^{−1}δ₁δ₂.
B(ω, 1) is reducible: an extension of St by the trivial character.

nodes.title: Classification of irreducible mod p representations of GL₂(ℚ_p)
nodes.statement: Let k be a finite extension of 𝔽_p (or 𝔽̄_p), and for 0 ≤ r ≤ p−1, χ : ℚ_p^× → k^× smooth and λ ∈ k, let W_{r,χ} = Sym^r k² ⊗ (χ∘det) as a KZ-module (p acting trivially), I(W_{r,χ}) = c-Ind_{KZ}^G W_{r,χ} with End_G = k[T] (Barthel–Livné operator T), and Π(r, λ, χ) = I(W_{r,χ})/(T − λ). (i) Π(r, λ, χ) is irreducible except for r = 0, λ = ±1 (an extension of St ⊗ (χμ_λ∘det) by χμ_λ∘det) and r = p−1, λ = ±1 (an extension of χμ_λ∘det by St ⊗ (χμ_λ∘det)). (ii) Every absolutely irreducible smooth k-representation of G is a Jordan–Hölder constituent of some Π(r, λ, χ); concretely the absolutely irreducible ones are: characters χ∘det; St ⊗ (χ∘det); irreducible principal series Ind_B^G(χ₁ ⊗ χ₂) with χ₁ ≠ χ₂; and supersingular Π(r, 0, χ). (iii) The only isomorphisms between supersingulars are Π(r, 0, χ) ≅ Π(r, 0, χμ_{−1}) ≅ Π(p−1−r, 0, χω^r) ≅ Π(p−1−r, 0, χω^rμ_{−1}); there are no intertwinings between supersingulars and principal-series constituents, nor between constituents of different principal series. (iv) Every irreducible smooth representation of G over 𝔽̄_p has a central character (Berger), is admissible and finitely presented, and is defined over a finite field; Gal(𝔽̄_p/k)-orbits of 𝔽̄_p-irreducibles correspond bijectively to irreducible k-representations.
hypotheses: F = ℚ_p: the irreducibility of I(σ)/(T) (Breuil) and finite presentation of supersingulars fail for F ≠ ℚ_p (R30.2/no-correspondence-beyond-qp).
proofSteps: Barthel–Livné: End_G(I(σ)) ≅ k[T], I(σ) free over k[T], every irreducible with central character is a quotient of some I(σ)/(T − λ), and the λ ≠ 0 quotients are principal series or their constituents (FiniteFlat R07.5).
Breuil: I(σ)/(T) is irreducible for F = ℚ_p (Breuil 2003, Théorème 1.1, via Corollaires 4.1.1 and 4.1.4) and the isomorphisms between them (Théorème 1.3).
Colmez Théorème III.3.2 and Proposition III.3.5 package (i)–(iii) in the notation Π(r, λ, χ).
(iv): Berger's central character theorem; admissibility and finite presentation of ordinary and supersingular irreducibles (CDN 2023 §1.2.3); Galois descent of irreducibles (CDN 2023 Lemma 1.7).
acceptance: The number of isomorphism classes of supersingular representations of GL₂(ℚ_p) over 𝔽̄_p with a fixed central character is finite, and over 𝔽̄_p they are in bijection with irreducible two-dimensional Galois representations with the matching determinant (Breuil Corollaire 1.4; R30.3/montreal-on-irreducibles).
For p = 2, Π(0, 0, χ) ≅ Π(1, 0, χ) (take r = 0, p−1−r = 1 and ω trivial).
Π(0, 1, 1) is reducible: trivial character as sub, Steinberg as quotient.

sources.locator: §III.3.1, Théorème III.3.2 and Proposition III.3.5, pp. 85–86
sources.match: Defines W_{r,χ} and Π(r, λ, χ), states that Π(r, λ, χ) is irreducible except for r ∈ {0, p−1} and λ = ±1, that every absolutely irreducible representation is a constituent of some Π(r, λ, χ), and lists the only intertwinings between supersingulars.

nodes.title: Irreducible mod ℓ representations of GL₂(ℤ_ℓ), U₀(ℓ) and Ũ₀(ℓ)
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be a prime, U₀(ℓ) = {(a b; c d) ∈ GL₂(ℤ_ℓ) : c ∈ ℓℤ_ℓ} and Ũ₀(ℓ) its normaliser in GL₂(ℚ_ℓ) modulo ℓ^ℤ, generated by U₀(ℓ) and w_ℓ = (0 1; ℓ 0). Over 𝔽̄_ℓ: (i) the irreducible continuous representations of GL₂(ℤ_ℓ) are σ_{n,m} = Sym^n(𝔽̄_ℓ²) ⊗ det^m with 0 ≤ n ≤ ℓ−1 and m ∈ ℤ/(ℓ−1); (ii) those of U₀(ℓ) are the characters σ'_{m₁,m₂} : (a b; ℓc d) ↦ ā^{m₁} d̄^{m₂}; (iii) those of Ũ₀(ℓ) (with ℓ acting trivially) are the two-dimensional inductions σ'_{{m₁,m₂},a} for m₁ ≠ m₂ (with −ℓ acting by a) and the characters σ'_{{m},a} extending σ'_{m,m} with w_ℓ acting by a.
hypotheses: ℓ prime (in the applications ℓ = p); representations over 𝔽̄_ℓ, continuous for the profinite topology, ℓ acting trivially on Ũ₀(ℓ)-representations.
proofSteps: (i): such a representation factors through GL₂(𝔽_ℓ) because the kernel K₁ is pro-ℓ; the irreducible 𝔽̄_ℓ[GL₂(𝔽_ℓ)]-modules are Sym^n ⊗ det^m (Serre weights, FiniteFlat R07.5).
(ii): U₀(ℓ) acts through its quotient by a pro-ℓ normal subgroup onto the torus (𝔽_ℓ^×)², an abelian group of order prime to ℓ.
(iii): Clifford theory for the index-two (modulo ℓ^ℤ) extension Ũ₀(ℓ) ⊃ U₀(ℓ)ℓ^ℤ, with w_ℓ swapping σ'_{m₁,m₂} and σ'_{m₂,m₁}.
acceptance: There are ℓ(ℓ−1) isomorphism classes in (i).
σ_{0,m} = det^m is one-dimensional; σ_{ℓ−1,0} has dimension ℓ.

nodes.title: What fails for GL₂(F) with F ≠ ℚ_p
nodes.statement: For a finite extension F ≠ ℚ_p of ℚ_p, the mod p theory of GL₂(F) differs from that of GL₂(ℚ_p) in ways that block the constructions of this roadmap: (i) supersingular representations of GL₂(F) over 𝔽̄_p are not finitely presented (Schraen, Wu); (ii) for F = ℚ_{p³} there are smooth irreducible k_L-representations of GL₂(F) that are not admissible, and a supersingular 𝔽_{p³}-representation with End = 𝔽_p which is not absolutely irreducible over any finite extension (Le); (iii) the quotients I(σ)/(T) are not irreducible and supersingular representations are not classified. Consequently nothing in this roadmap asserts a p-adic or mod p correspondence for GL₂(F), F ≠ ℚ_p: every theorem is stated for G = GL₂(ℚ_p).
hypotheses: F/ℚ_p finite, F ≠ ℚ_p.
proofSteps: (i) is CDN 2023 Théorème 1.27, citing Schraen and Wu; (ii) is CDN 2023 Remarques 1.8 and 1.28, citing Le; (iii) is the CDN 2023 §1.2.1 description, which leaves supersingulars of GL₂(F) unclassified.
Colmez's Remarque 0.8(iii) records that standard presentations, which the construction of D(Π) needs, are expected to fail for GL₂(F), F ≠ ℚ_p.
acceptance: The roadmap's statements carry the hypothesis F = ℚ_p wherever they use R30.2/modp-irreducibles, R30.3/montreal-functor or R30.5/blocks.

sources.locator: §1.2.1, pp. 14–15; Remarque 1.8, p. 16; Théorème 1.27 and Remarque 1.28, p. 25
sources.match: For F ≠ ℚ_p the supersingular representations are not finitely presented (Schraen, Wu); Le constructed irreducible non-admissible representations of GL₂(ℚ_{p³}) and a supersingular with End = 𝔽_p that is not absolutely irreducible.
Breuil–Paškūnas suggest that the existence of standard presentations fails in characteristic p for GL₂ of a nontrivial extension of ℚ_p.

nodes.title: The G-module D ⊠_δ ℙ¹
nodes.statement: Let D be an étale (φ,Γ)-module over O_E (torsion or free) or over E, and δ : ℚ_p^× → O_L^× a continuous unitary character. On D ⊠ ℤ_p^× = D^{ψ=0} there is an involution w_δ, the limit of Σ_{i ∈ ℤ_p^× mod p^n} δ(i^{−1})(1+T)^i σ_{−i^2}(φ^nψ^n((1+T)^{−i^{−1}}z)). Put D ⊠_δ ℙ¹ = {z = (z₁, z₂) ∈ D × D : Res_{ℤ_p^×}(z₂) = w_δ(Res_{ℤ_p^×}(z₁))}. There is a unique action of G on D ⊠_δ ℙ¹ such that Res_U(g·z) = H_g(Res_{g^{−1}U ∩ ℤ_p}(z₁)) + H_{gw}(Res_{(gw)^{−1}U ∩ pℤ_p}(z₂)) for every compact open U ⊂ ℚ_p, with the explicit skeleton: w(z₁, z₂) = (z₂, z₁); (a 0; 0 a) acts by δ(a); (a 0; 0 1), a ∈ ℤ_p^×, by ((a 0; 0 1)z₁, δ(a)(a^{−1} 0; 0 1)z₂); and the formulas for (p 0; 0 1) and (1 b; 0 1), b ∈ pℤ_p. Restrictions Res_U : D ⊠_δ ℙ¹ → D ⊠ U and Res_{ℚ_p} : D ⊠_δ ℙ¹ → D ⊠_δ ℚ_p are G- resp. B-compatible; Res_{ℤ_p}z = z₁ and Res_{ℤ_p}(w·z) = z₂. For D⁰(ℤ_p) = E^♮ the construction is the dual B(δ)* of the space of continuous φ on ℚ_p with x ↦ δ(x)φ(1/x) continuous at 0, with g·φ = φ ⋆ g^{−1}, (φ ⋆ (a b; c d))(x) = δ(cx+d)φ((ax+b)/(cx+d)). Twisting: (D ⊠_δ ℙ¹) ⊗ (η∘det) ≅ (D ⊗ η) ⊠_{δη²} ℙ¹, and there is a perfect G-equivariant pairing { , }_{ℙ¹} between Ď ⊠_{δ^{−1}} ℙ¹ and D ⊠_δ ℙ¹.
hypotheses: D étale; δ unitary continuous; the construction is analytic in (D, δ) over S ⊗̂ O_E for S a quotient of O_L[[X₁,…,X_d]] (Remarque 0.18(iv)).
proofSteps: Define w_δ on D^{ψ=0} by the limit formula; convergence and the involution property are Colmez's Lemme II.1.2 and Remarque II.1.3.

Define the action of the generators by the skeleton formulas and prove uniqueness and existence of the G-action from the Res_U formula (Colmez Théorème II.1.4, p. 47), using P(ℚ_p), Z and w generating G (R30.1/gl2qp-subgroups) and the P(ℚ_p)-module D ⊠ ℚ_p (R30.1/boxtimes-qp).
The measure case: the restriction maps to ℤ_p and to w·ℤ_p identify B(δ)* with D⁰(ℤ_p) ⊠_δ ℙ¹, the pairs (μ₁, μ₂) with Res_{ℤ_p^×}μ₂ = w_δ(Res_{ℤ_p^×}μ₁) (Colmez §5, p. 10).
Twisting (Colmez §II.1.3) and the pairing (Théorème II.1.13) from the residue pairing on Ď × D (R30.1/tate-dual).
acceptance: The centre acts through δ.
Res_{ℤ_p} and Res_{ℤ_p}∘w recover (z₁, z₂).
{ , }_{ℙ¹} is perfect and G-equivariant.

nodes.title: Colmez's Montreal functor Π ↦ D(Π), V(Π)
nodes.statement: For Π ∈ Rep^{tors}G choose a finite length K-stable W ⊂ Π generating Π (W(Π) ≠ ∅; Π = I(W)/R(W, Π) is a standard presentation, which exists for every Π, Colmez Théorème III.3.1). Let I^Π_{ℤ_p}(W) be the O_L-span of the (p^n a; 0 1)·W with a + p^nℤ_p ⊂ ℤ_p, D^♮_W(Π) its Pontryagin dual (a quotient of Π^∨), and D⁺_W(Π) ⊂ Π^∨ the μ vanishing on (p^n a; 0 1)·W for a + p^nℤ_p ⊄ ℤ_p. These are Γ-modules over O_E⁺ (T acting by (1 1; 0 1) − 1, σ_a by (a 0; 0 1)), D⁺_W(Π) is a (φ,Γ)-module over O_E⁺ with φ = (p 0; 0 1), and D(Π) := O_E ⊗ D⁺_W(Π) ≅ O_E ⊗ D^♮_W(Π) is independent of W, with β_{ℤ_p} : Π^∨ → D(Π). Then D is an exact contravariant functor Rep^{tors}G → ΦΓ^et_tors, extended to Rep_{O_L}G by inverse limits and to Rep_L G by ⊗ L. V(Π) := the Tate dual of V(D(Π)) defines an exact covariant functor Rep^{tors}G → Rep_tors G_{ℚ_p}, Rep_{O_L}G → Rep_{O_L}G_{ℚ_p}, Rep_L G → Rep_L G_{ℚ_p}, with V(Π ⊗ (δ∘det)) = V(Π) ⊗ δ, and V(Π) = MF(Π)(ε) for Emerton's normalisation MF. Paškūnas's variant on the dual category: V̌(M) := V(M^∨)^∨(ζε) for M ∈ C_{G,ζ}(O), extended to pseudo-compact objects by limits.
hypotheses: Π ∈ Rep^{tors}G (smooth, admissible, finite length, central character) or a lattice / Banach representation residually in it.
F = ℚ_p (standard presentations; R30.2/no-correspondence-beyond-qp).
proofSteps: Existence of standard presentations (Colmez Théorème III.3.1), reduced by dévissage to irreducibles via the classification R30.2/modp-irreducibles.
Construction of D^♮_W, D⁺_W and their module structures (Colmez §IV.1, Proposition IV.1.11–IV.1.12: β ∘ (p^{−1} 0; 0 1) = ψ ∘ β).

Finite length of D(Π) for irreducible Π: explicit computation of D^♮_{W_r}(Π(r, λ)) as k_E⁺ ⊕ k_E⁺ (λ = 0) or k_E⁺ ⊕ k_E⁺/T (λ ≠ 0) (Théorème IV.2.1); exactness by Proposition IV.2.12 and dévissage (Théorème IV.2.13).
Passage to V and its exactness via Fontaine's equivalence (Théorème IV.2.14; R30.1/fontaine-functor-convention).
Comparison with MF: Emerton defines MF(π) as the Pontryagin dual of V(D(π)) (lg §3.2 and footnote 6), Colmez as the Tate dual; they differ by ε.
acceptance: V(χ∘det) = 0 (Théorème 0.10(i)).
V is exact: a short exact sequence in Rep^{tors}G gives a short exact sequence of Galois representations.
V(Π ⊗ (δ∘det)) = V(Π) ⊗ δ.

sources.locator: Introduction §6, Théorèmes 0.7 and 0.9, pp. 11–13; §IV.1–IV.2, Théorèmes IV.2.1, IV.2.13 and IV.2.14, pp. 97–103

nodes.statement: (i) V(δ∘det) = 0; (ii) V(St ⊗ (δ∘det)) = k_L(ωδ); (iii) V(B(δ₁, δ₂)) = k_L(δ₁) for B(δ₁, δ₂) = Ind_B^G(δ₂ ⊗ δ₁ω^{−1}); (iv) for Π supersingular, V(Π) is irreducible of dimension 2 over k_L; precisely V(Π(r, 0, δ) ⊗ (−1)^{v_p(x)}) = V(r, δ), Colmez's irreducible atome galoisien. nodes.title: Reconstruction of Π from D(Π): β_{ℙ¹} and the contragredient
nodes.statement: Let Π ∈ Rep^{tors}G have no finite quotient, central character δ_Π, D = D(Π) and δ = δ_Π^{−1}. (i) β_{ℚ_p} : Π^∨ → D ⊠_δ ℚ_p, μ ↦ (β_{ℤ_p}((p^n 0; 0 1)μ))_n, is B-equivariant with kernel (Π^∨)^U, image in D^♯ ⊠ ℚ_p containing D^♮ ⊠ ℚ_p, with equality when Π has no finite subrepresentation. (ii) β_{ℙ¹} : μ ↦ (β_{ℤ_p}(μ), β_{ℤ_p}(wμ)) is an injective G-equivariant map Π^∨ → D ⊠_δ ℙ¹ with Res_{ℚ_p} ∘ β_{ℙ¹} = β_{ℚ_p}, landing in {z : Res_{ℚ_p}z ∈ D^♯ ⊠_δ ℚ_p}; the subspace D^♮ ⊠_δ ℙ¹ = {z : Res_{ℚ_p}z ∈ D^♮ ⊠_δ ℚ_p} is a G-stable compact open containing the image of the orthogonal of Π^{SL₂(ℚ_p)} with finite index, and its dual is equivalent to Π. (iii) The contragredient Π̌ := (D ⊠_δ ℙ¹)/β_{ℙ¹}(Π^∨) lies in Rep^{tors}G, has no finite quotient, and its contragredient is Π. Examples: B(δ₁, δ₂)ˇ ≅ B(δ₂, δ₁) ⊗ δ_Π^{−1}; Šť is a non-split extension of B(1, ω) by 1; Π̌ ≅ Π ⊗ δ_Π^{−1} for supersingular Π.
hypotheses: Π ∈ Rep^{tors}G without finite quotient; F = ℚ_p.
proofSteps: β_{ℚ_p}: Proposition 0.12 and §IV.3.1 (Lemme IV.3.1: the kernel of α_{ℤ_p,W} has finite length).
The key identity β_{ℤ_p^×} ∘ w = w_δ ∘ β_{ℤ_p^×} (Proposition IV.4.2) gives that β_{ℙ¹} lands in D ⊠_δ ℙ¹ and is G-equivariant (Théorème IV.4.7).
G-stability and duality of D^♮ ⊠_δ ℙ¹ (Théorème IV.4.1) and the contragredient statements (Théorème 0.14, §IV.4.5, Proposition IV.4.18).
acceptance: For Π supersingular, Π̌ ≅ Π ⊗ δ_Π^{−1}.
The contragredient of the contragredient is Π.

sources.locator: Proposition 0.12, Théorèmes 0.13 and 0.14, Exemples 0.15, p. 14; Théorème IV.4.1, p. 106; Proposition IV.4.2 and Théorème IV.4.7, pp. 107–110

nodes.title: Colmez's representation Π(D) and the correspondence V ↦ Π(V)
nodes.statement: Let D ∈ ΦΓ^et(E) be of rank 2, α_D the character of ∧²D, δ_D = (x|x|)^{−1}α_D (R30.1/tate-dual), and D ⊠ ℙ¹ := D ⊠_{δ_D} ℙ¹ (central character δ_D). Put D^♮ ⊠ ℙ¹ = {z ∈ D ⊠ ℙ¹ : Res_{ℚ_p}(z) ∈ D^♮ ⊠ ℚ_p} and, when it is G-stable, Π(D) := (D ⊠ ℙ¹)/(D^♮ ⊠ ℙ¹). For a two-dimensional L-representation V of G_{ℚ_p}, Π(V) := Π(D(V)). The same recipe applies to D ∈ ΦΓ^et(O_E) and to torsion D, compatibly with reduction mod p up to finite length pieces, and in families over S ⊗̂ O_E. The construction does not presuppose the correspondence: Π(D) is defined from D alone, and the identities D(Π(D)) = Ď and V(Π(V)) = V are theorems (R30.3/colmez-correspondence).
hypotheses: D étale of rank 2 over E (or O_E, torsion); G-stability of D^♮ ⊠ ℙ¹ is the theorem R30.3/colmez-correspondence.
proofSteps: Define δ_D and D ⊠ ℙ¹ from R30.3/boxtimes-p1 and R30.1/tate-dual.
D^♮ ⊠ ℙ¹ is defined through Res_{ℚ_p} and D^♮ ⊠ ℚ_p (R30.1/psi-and-treillis, R30.1/boxtimes-qp); it is compact open in D ⊠ ℙ¹.
Π(D) is the quotient; its topology is the quotient topology, and for D over E it is an L-Banach space with the unit ball the image of the integral version.
acceptance: For D of rank 2 with det V(D) = χ, δ_D = 1 and Π(D) has trivial central character.
Π(D ⊗ η) = Π(D) ⊗ (η∘det) for a unitary character η.

nodes.title: Colmez's theorem: Π(D) is irreducible and D(Π(D)) = Ď
nodes.statement: Let D ∈ ΦΓ^et(E) be irreducible of rank 2. (i) D^♮ ⊠ ℙ¹ is stable under G. (ii) Π(D) = (D ⊠ ℙ¹)/(D^♮ ⊠ ℙ¹) is a topologically irreducible object of Rep_L G, D^♮ ⊠ ℙ¹ ≅ Π(D)* ⊗ δ_D, so there is an exact sequence 0 → Π(D)* ⊗ δ_D → D ⊠ ℙ¹ → Π(D) → 0. (iii) D(Π(D)) = Ď; equivalently V(Π(V)) ≅ V for every absolutely irreducible two-dimensional V. The proof of (i) is by analytic continuation from a Zariski-dense set of crystabelline or trianguline points; Colmez's text records the needed Zariski density for p ≥ 5, for p = 3 except for twists of extensions of k_L by k_L(ω) and of ind ω₂² (those two cases following from Böckle's computation of mod 3 deformation rings), and for p = 2 when V^{ss} is not the sum of two equal characters (a computation of Chenevier); Colmez–Dospinescu–Paškūnas (characteristic zero methods, valid for all p) give the bijection of R30.3/cdp-correspondence, which includes V(Π) ≅ V for all absolutely irreducible V.
hypotheses: D irreducible of rank 2 over E; p any prime with the case division recorded in the statement.
proofSteps: (i) ⇒ (ii), (iii): Corollaire II.2.12 and Remarque II.3.2(i): G-stability gives Π(D) ∈ Rep_L G with D(Π(D)) = Ď, and the identification D^♮ ⊠ ℙ¹ ≅ Π(D)* ⊗ δ_D follows from Ď ≅ D ⊗ δ_D^{−1}.

(i) by analytic continuation: the construction is analytic in families (Théorème II.3.3, the family version of (i)) and the crystabelline (or trianguline) points are Zariski-dense in the deformation space of each residual representation (Colmez, Introduction footnote 7, citing his trianguline paper and Kisin's Astérisque article, Böckle for two residual types at p = 3 and Chenevier for p = 2).
Crystabelline points: G-stability is checked by explicit computation for crystabelline D (Colmez §II.3.3, pp. 64–69), or alternatively via Corollaire IV.4.13.
Irreducibility: Π(D) has irreducible reduction for supersingular reductions; for the general case use V(Π(D)) irreducible of dimension 2 and exactness of V.
acceptance: For V crystalline irreducible with distinct Frobenius eigenvalues, Π(V) is the Berger–Breuil completion.
V(Π(V)) ≅ V.

sources.locator: Théorème 0.17, Remarque 0.18 and footnote 7, pp. 15–17; Théorème II.3.1, Remarque II.3.2 and Théorème II.3.3, pp. 62–63

nodes.title: The p-adic local Langlands correspondence for GL₂(ℚ_p)
nodes.statement: (i) (Colmez–Dospinescu–Paškūnas; Paškūnas for p ≥ 5) V induces a bijection between isomorphism classes of absolutely irreducible non-ordinary Π ∈ Ban^{adm}_G(L) and absolutely irreducible two-dimensional continuous L-representations of G_{ℚ_p}; its inverse is V ↦ Π(V). (ii) Every absolutely irreducible Π ∈ Ban^{adm}_G(L) is residually of finite length, and after replacing L by its quadratic unramified extension Π̄^{ss} is absolutely irreducible supersingular or a subrepresentation of some π{χ₁, χ₂}. (iii) If Π is absolutely irreducible non-ordinary with central character δ, then det V(Π) = δε. (iv) An object of Ban^{adm}_G(L) has finite length iff it is residually of finite length. (v) dim_L V(Π) ≤ 2 for every absolutely irreducible Π, with equality iff Π is non-ordinary. (vi) For absolutely irreducible non-ordinary Π₁, Π₂: V(Π₁) ≅ V(Π₂) ⇒ Π₁ ≅ Π₂, and Hom_{L[P]}^{cont}(Π₁, Π₂) = Hom_{L[G]}^{cont}(Π₁, Π₂). (vii) For p ≥ 5 (Paškūnas): if Π is absolutely irreducible with central character and Θ an open bounded G-stable lattice then Θ ⊗ k has finite length and either is absolutely irreducible supersingular or has semisimplification inside (Ind_P^G χ₁ ⊗ χ₂ω^{−1})^{ss} ⊕ (Ind_P^G χ₂ ⊗ χ₁ω^{−1})^{ss}, with equality iff Π is non-ordinary.
hypotheses: L/ℚ_p finite; Π admissible unitary with central character (automatic for absolutely irreducible Π by Dospinescu–Schraen's Schur lemma).
proofSteps: p ≥ 5: Paškūnas's projective envelope method, showing that End(P̃) surjects onto, and then equals, a deformation ring (R30.5/paskunas-endomorphism-rings), with Theorem 1.3 deduced from Berger–Breuil, Colmez and Kisin.

All p: CDP's characteristic zero argument — residual finiteness from the blocks for p = 2 (Paškūnas), Schur's lemma for Banach representations (Dospinescu–Schraen), the locally analytic vectors of unitary principal series, and the infinitesimal action on locally analytic vectors (CDP §1.1–1.5).
(iii) from the explicit construction of Π(V) and local class field theory (R30.1/character-dictionary).
acceptance: For V crystabelline irreducible, Π(V) is the Berger–Breuil completion and V(Π(V)) = V.
The ordinary Π (characters, Ŝp ⊗ η, unitary principal series) have dim V(Π) ≤ 1.

nodes.title: Injectivity of V on Ext¹ of atoms
nodes.statement: Let Π ∈ Rep_{k_L}G be an automorphic atom of length at most 3 (the reduction of a unitary principal series or of Π(V), in Colmez's list). Then V induces an injection Ext¹_G(Π, Π) → Ext¹_{G_{ℚ_p}}(V(Π), V(Π)) (extensions with central character); for supersingular atoms this is an isomorphism onto the extensions with determinant fixed. Kisin's deformation-theoretic argument deduces from this injectivity that V induces a closed immersion of deformation spaces, which is an isomorphism because its image contains the Zariski-dense trianguline points.
hypotheses: Atoms of length ≤ 3 (the cases of length 4 occur only for p = 2, 3 and are not covered by Colmez's Théorème VII.5.2); central characters fixed.
proofSteps: Compute Ext¹ on the G-side with the Jacquet functor and the extensions of §VII.2 (Colmez §VII.5.1–VII.5.2), and on the Galois side with (φ,Γ)-module cohomology (Appendix VIII).
Kisin's argument: injectivity on tangent spaces gives a closed immersion of deformation functors; trianguline density gives surjectivity (Colmez, Introduction §13.2).
acceptance: For Π supersingular with V(Π) = ρ̄, dim Ext¹_G(Π, Π)_ζ = dim Ext¹(ρ̄, ρ̄)_{det}.

sources.match: Records Kisin's strategy (Ext¹ injectivity plus Zariski density of trianguline points) and proves the injectivity of Ext¹(Π, Π) → Ext¹(V(Π), V(Π)) for automorphic atoms of length at most 3.

nodes.title: Locally analytic vectors of Π(D)
nodes.statement: Let D ∈ ΦΓ^et(E) be irreducible of rank 2 and Π = Π(D). (i) D† ⊠ ℙ¹ = {(z₁, z₂) ∈ D ⊠ ℙ¹ : z₁, z₂ ∈ D†} is G-stable and its image in Π(D) is Π(D)^{an}; indeed Π^{an} = (D† ⊠ ℙ¹)/L·(D^♮ ⊠ ℙ¹). (ii) The G-action extends continuously to D_rig ⊠ ℙ¹, with an exact sequence 0 → (Π(D)^{an})* ⊗ δ_D → D_rig ⊠ ℙ¹ → Π(D)^{an} → 0, and D^♮_rig ⊠ ℙ¹ = (Π̌^{an})*. (iii) (Colmez–Dospinescu) Π(D) is the universal unitary completion of Π(D)^{an}.
hypotheses: D irreducible of rank 2 over E.
proofSteps: (i): D† ⊠ ℤ_p^× is w-stable, proved through Fontaine's heart C(D) = (1−φ)D^{ψ=1}, a free Λ[1/p]-module of rank 2 with w(C(D)) = C'(D) (Proposition V.2.1) and D† ⊠ ℤ_p^× = E†(Γ) ⊗_Λ C(D).
(ii): Colmez Théorème V.2.20, using the duality { , }_{ℙ¹} extended to D_rig ⊠ ℙ¹ (Proposition V.2.10).
(iii): Colmez–Dospinescu Théorème 0.2 (R30.2/universal-unitary-completion).
acceptance: Π(D)^{an} is dense in Π(D).
For D crystabelline, Π(D)^{an} contains the locally algebraic principal series of R30.4.

nodes.title: The algebraic and smooth factors LL(V) and Alg(V) of a de Rham V
nodes.statement: Let V be a two-dimensional L-representation of G_{ℚ_p} that is de Rham with distinct Hodge–Tate weights a < b (PadicHodgeTheory R06.2/hodge-tate-weight-convention as used by Colmez). Let D_pst(V) be its (φ, N, G_{ℚ_p})-module and WD(V) the attached Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representation (PadicHodgeTheory R06.3/weil-deligne-parameter). Put LL(V) := LL(D_pst(V)), the smooth representation of R30.1/classical-normalisation-bridge (irreducible except for the N = 0, δ ⊕ δ|·| case, where it is the reducible principal series), Alg(V) := W_{a, b−a} = Sym^{b−a−1}L² ⊗ det^a, and LL(V, a, b) := LL(V) ⊗ Alg(V), a locally algebraic representation of G. For a (φ, N, G_{ℚ_p})-module M and a < b, LL(M, a, b) := LL(M) ⊗ W_{a,b−a} depends on M and (a, b) only, not on the Hodge filtration. The set F of admissible filtrations on M_dR with jumps a < b is ℙ¹(M_dR) minus 0, 1 or 2 points when nonempty, and for ℒ ∈ F, D_ℒ denotes the étale (φ,Γ)-module of the weakly admissible filtered module (M, ℒ).
hypotheses: V two-dimensional de Rham with distinct Hodge–Tate weights; the weight convention of Colmez (Théorème 0.20) is recorded with its dictionary to PadicHodgeTheory R06.2.
proofSteps: WD(V) from D_pst(V) by Fontaine's recipe (PadicHodgeTheory R06.3/fontaine-weil-deligne-functor, using the p-adic monodromy theorem R06.3/p-adic-monodromy-theorem).
LL(M) from R30.1/classical-normalisation-bridge.

Independence of the filtration is by construction; the parametrisation of admissible filtrations by ℙ¹(M_dR) minus finitely many points is the Colmez–Fontaine theorem in rank 2 (PadicHodgeTheory R06.2/colmez-fontaine-bigness-criterion) applied to lines in M_dR.
acceptance: For V crystalline with distinct Frobenius eigenvalues α, β (α/β ≠ p^{±1}) and weights a < b, LL(V) is the unramified principal series attached to the two unramified characters μ_α, μ_β, and Alg(V) = Sym^{b−a−1} ⊗ det^a.

nodes.title: Locally algebraic vectors of Π(V): Colmez's theorem
nodes.statement: Let D ∈ ΦΓ^et(E) be irreducible of rank 2, V = V(D) and Π = Π(D). (i) Π^{alg} ≠ 0 iff D is de Rham with distinct Hodge–Tate weights a < b; Π^{alg} = 0 if D is not de Rham; if Π^{alg} ≠ 0 then D is almost de Rham with distinct weights and Π^{alg} = Π^{lc} ⊗ (Sym^{b−a−1} ⊗ det^a) with Π^{lc} smooth admissible. (ii) Π^{alg} depends, up to isomorphism, only on D_pst as (φ, N, G_{ℚ_p})-module and on (a, b), not on the filtration. (iii) If dim J₀(Π^{alg}) = 2 then D is crystabelline and Π^{alg} = LL(D_pst) ⊗ Alg; if dim J₀(Π^{alg}) = 1, D is a locally algebraic twist of a semistable non-crystalline module and Π^{alg} = LL(D_pst) ⊗ Alg; if dim J₀(Π^{alg}) = 0, D is de Rham but becomes semistable over no abelian extension. (iv) Π^{alg} is supersingular iff V is not trianguline. (v) In all cases, Π(V)^{alg} ≅ LL(V) ⊗ Alg(V) (with Emerton's normalisations Sym^{a−b−1} ⊗ det^{b+1} ⊗ π_p(V) for his weights a > b); in the potentially crystalline non-crystabelline (supercuspidal) case this identification is proved only by a global argument (Emerton, lg §7.4), recorded as gap G1.
hypotheses: D irreducible of rank 2 over E; for (v) in the supercuspidal case, the global input of gap G1.
proofSteps: (i) non-de Rham: the image of Π^{alg} in D_rig ⊠ ℤ_p^× lies in R(Γ) ⊗ C_e(D), which is w-stable iff D is de Rham (Proposition 0.26, Théorème 0.25 = VI.6.8, via Kato's explicit reciprocity law), giving VI.6.13.
(i) de Rham: nonvanishing by Lemme VI.6.19 (Théorème VI.6.18); the type (ℓ, k) structure by Proposition VI.5.1 and the Kirillov model (Théorème VI.5.7).
(ii): Théorème VI.6.42, comparing D_ℒ for varying filtrations inside N_rig ⊠ ℙ¹.
(iii): Théorème VI.6.50, from the Jacquet module J₀ and D_crab (Théorème VI.6.30, Proposition VI.6.33).
(iv): Remarque VI.6.51(i) with the trianguline classification (R30.1/trianguline-representation).

(v): crystabelline and semistable-twist cases from (iii); the remaining case by Emerton's global argument via (ii) — choose a modular V' with the same D_pst and weights (Emerton lg §7.4) — recorded as gap G1 because its inputs (completed cohomology of modular curves, the weight part of Serre's conjecture) lie outside this roadmap and downstream of R30.6.
acceptance: For V de Rham with Hodge–Tate weights 0 and 1, Alg(V) is trivial and Π(V)^{lisse} = Π(V)^{alg} = LL(V) (CDN 2020 §0.2).
For V crystalline irreducible with weights 0 < k−1, Π(V)^{alg} is the locally algebraic principal series LL(V) ⊗ Sym^{k−2}.
For V semistable non-crystalline with weights 0 < k−1, Π(V)^{alg} = (St ⊗ Sym^{k−2}) ⊗ δ for the smooth δ of D_crab.
For V not de Rham, Π(V)^{alg} = 0 while Π(V)^{an} is dense.

sources.locator: Théorèmes 0.20–0.21, p. 17; Théorème 0.25 and Proposition 0.26, p. 20; Théorème VI.5.7, p. 167; Théorèmes VI.6.13 and VI.6.18, pp. 177–178; Théorème VI.6.42, p. 189; Théorème VI.6.50 and Remarque VI.6.51, pp. 192–193
sources.match: Π(D)^{alg} is nonzero iff D is de Rham with distinct weights, with Π^{alg} = Π^{lc} ⊗ Sym^{b−a−1} ⊗ det^a; Π^{alg} is independent of the filtration; LL(D_pst) = Π^{lc} in the crystabelline and semistable-twist cases; supersingular Π^{alg} iff V not trianguline; the remaining case uses Emerton's global work.

B(V)^{l.alg} ≅ Sym^{a−b−1} ⊗ det^{b+1} ⊗ π_p(V) for de Rham V with weights a > b; the potentially crystalline non-crystabelline case is proved by choosing a modular representation with the same Weil–Deligne type and weights and computing in completed cohomology.

The classification of completions uses Emerton's local-global compatibility; the authors note that a purely local proof is available for principal series and Steinberg types but not for supercuspidal ones.
Even their purely local construction of Kisin rings has a hidden global ingredient: Emerton's local-global compatibility ensures that M and LL(M) correspond under the classical correspondence.
For V de Rham of dimension 2 with weights 0 and 1, LL(V) = Π(V)^{lisse}, recovered from Π(V) by taking locally constant vectors.

nodes.title: Berger–Breuil: unitary completions of locally algebraic principal series
nodes.statement: Let V be an absolutely irreducible two-dimensional L-representation of G_{ℚ_p} that becomes crystalline over an abelian extension of ℚ_p and is φ-semisimple, with Hodge–Tate weights a < b. Let B(V) be the p-adic completion of the locally algebraic representation Alg(V) ⊗ Lisse(V) (a locally algebraic principal series) with respect to a G-stable finitely generated O-lattice. Then B(V) is nonzero, topologically irreducible and admissible, and it is the universal unitary completion of Alg(V) ⊗ Lisse(V); its dual is identified with the ψ-limit (lim_ψ D(V))_b. With Colmez's construction, B(V) ≅ Π(V).
hypotheses: V crystabelline (crystalline over an abelian extension), φ-semisimple, absolutely irreducible; p odd in Berger–Breuil's source; the exceptional cases α = β|·|^{±1} handled by Paškūnas for p > 2 (Emerton lg footnote 9).
proofSteps: Construct B(V) as the completion of the locally algebraic principal series (R30.2/universal-unitary-completion).
Identify (lim_ψ D(V))_b with B(V)* (Berger–Breuil Théorème 5.2.7) using the (φ,Γ)-module of the crystabelline V and the Amice transform (R30.1/fontaine-functor-convention).
Nonvanishing, topological irreducibility and admissibility: Corollaires 5.3.1–5.3.3.
B(V) ≅ Π(V): compare Théorème 5.2.7 with Colmez's Π(D)* ≅ D^♮ ⊠ ℙ¹ ⊗ δ_D^{−1} (R30.3/colmez-correspondence) as in Kisin's proof of Theorem (1.2.8).
acceptance: For V crystalline irreducible with Hodge–Tate weights 0, k−1 and distinct Frobenius eigenvalues, B(V) is the completion of LL(V) ⊗ Sym^{k−2}, LL(V) the unramified principal series of R30.4/locally-algebraic-type.
B(V)^{alg} = Alg(V) ⊗ Lisse(V).

sources.locator: Introduction, pp. 2–3 (main Théorème); Théorème 5.2.7, p. 51; Corollaires 5.3.1–5.3.3, p. 52
sources.match: For V absolutely irreducible, crystalline over an abelian extension and φ-semisimple, B(V) — the completion of Alg(V) ⊗ Lisse(V) — is nonzero, topologically irreducible and admissible; its dual is the ψ-limit of D(V).

sources.locator: Theorem (1.2.8) and its proof, p. 9 of the author's preprint
sources.match: For V irreducible of abelian type the lattice required by Hypothesis (1.2.6) is the Berger–Breuil completion, matched with Colmez's construction by comparing Berger–Breuil Théorème 5.2.7 with Colmez's results.

nodes.title: Henniart's K-types σ(τ), σ^cr(τ) and σ(w, τ)
nodes.statement: Let τ : I_{ℚ_p} → GL₂(L) be a representation with open kernel that extends to W_{ℚ_p} (an inertial type). Henniart's theorem: there is a unique smooth irreducible representation σ(τ) (resp. σ^cr(τ)) of K = GL₂(ℤ_p) on an L-vector space such that for every smooth absolutely irreducible infinite-dimensional representation π of G, Hom_K(σ(τ), π) ≠ 0 (resp. Hom_K(σ^cr(τ), π) ≠ 0) iff LL(π)|_{I_{ℚ_p}} ≅ τ (resp. and the monodromy N = 0), LL being the classical correspondence of R30.1/classical-normalisation-bridge. σ(τ) ≅ σ^cr(τ) except for scalar τ ≅ χ ⊕ χ, where σ(τ) ≅ s̃t ⊗ (χ∘det) (s̃t the Steinberg representation of GL₂(𝔽_p) inflated to K) and σ^cr(τ) ≅ χ∘det. For a Hodge type w = (a, b) with b > a put σ(w, τ) = σ(τ) ⊗ Sym^{b−a−1}L² ⊗ det^a and σ^cr(w, τ) likewise; Kisin writes σ(k, τ) = σ(τ) ⊗ Sym^{k−2}L² for w = (0, k−1). For a K-stable O-lattice Θ ⊂ σ(w, τ), σ̄(w, τ) := (Θ/ϖΘ)^{ss} is independent of Θ, and m_σ(w, τ) (resp. m^cr_σ(w, τ)) is the multiplicity of an irreducible smooth k-representation σ of K in σ̄(w, τ) (resp. σ̄^cr(w, τ)).
hypotheses: τ of Galois type; the classical correspondence normalised as in R30.1/classical-normalisation-bridge (Kisin §1.1: central character τ̃|_{ℚ_p^×}).
proofSteps: Henniart's appendix to Breuil–Mézard constructs σ(τ) case by case (principal series types by induction from the Iwahori, supercuspidal types from GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R16.2/henniart-unicity) and proves uniqueness.
The scalar-type exception: for τ = χ ⊕ χ, the unramified principal series twisted by χ contains χ∘det while St ⊗ χ contains only s̃t ⊗ χ, which separates N = 0 from N ≠ 0.
Independence of σ̄(w, τ) from Θ: Brauer–Nesbitt for the finite group K/K_n through which σ(w, τ) factors modulo ϖ.
acceptance: For τ trivial: σ^cr(1) is trivial and σ(1) = s̃t, so m_σ(w, 1) counts constituents of s̃t ⊗ Sym^{b−a−1} ⊗ det^a mod ϖ.
For w = (0, 1) and τ trivial, σ̄^cr(w, τ) is the trivial representation of K.

sources.match: States Henniart's existence and uniqueness of σ(τ) and σ^cr(τ) characterised by Hom_K(σ(τ), π) ≠ 0 iff LL(π)|_I ≅ τ (and N = 0 for σ^cr), the scalar-type exception s̃t ⊗ χ versus χ, σ(w, τ) = σ(τ) ⊗ Sym^{b−a−1} ⊗ det^a, its semisimplified reduction and the multiplicities m_σ(w, τ), m^cr_σ(w, τ).
Recalls Henniart's σ(τ) from the appendix to Breuil–Mézard with the classical correspondence normalised by the central character, and sets σ(k, τ) = σ(τ) ⊗ Sym^{k−2}E².

nodes.title: Kisin's Hypothesis (1.2.6): lattices containing the K-type
nodes.statement: Let p be odd, k ≥ 2, τ : I_{ℚ_p} → GL₂(E) an inertial type of Galois type, ψ a continuous character with ψ|_{I} compatible with τ, and σ(k, τ) = σ(τ) ⊗ Sym^{k−2}E² the Henniart–Breuil–Mézard K-type (R30.4/henniart-types). For every finite E'/E and every two-dimensional E'-representation V of G_{ℚ_p} that is potentially semistable of type τ with Hodge–Tate weights 0, k−1 and determinant ψ·χ_cyc (Kisin's type (k, τ, ψ)), there exist an admissible O_{E'}-lattice Θ (p-adically complete and separated O[G]-module with Θ/p^n of finite length and admissible) with central character ψ such that V(Θ) ⊗ ℚ_p ≅ V, and a K-equivariant inclusion σ(k, τ) ↪ Θ ⊗ ℚ_p. Proven: for τ of abelian type (τ extends to an abelian representation of W_{ℚ_p}) by Kisin's Theorem (1.2.8); for every de Rham type by Emerton (lg Theorem 3.3.22) together with Colmez's Théorème VI.6.50 (crystabelline and semistable cases) and R30.4/locally-algebraic-vectors, the supercuspidal types depending on gap G1.
hypotheses: p odd (Kisin §1.0); types of Galois type; V of type (k, τ, ψ) in Kisin's sense (1.1).
For non-abelian (supercuspidal) types the statement rests on R30.4/locally-algebraic-vectors (v) and therefore on gap G1.
proofSteps: Take Θ an open bounded G-stable lattice in Π(V) (R30.3/pi-of-D) with central character ψ, so V(Θ) ⊗ ℚ_p ≅ V (R30.3/colmez-correspondence; for reducible V use the lattices P(χ₁, χ₂) in continuous principal series, Kisin Lemma (1.2.10)).
Π(V)^{alg} ≅ LL(V) ⊗ Alg(V) (R30.4/locally-algebraic-vectors), and Alg(V) = Sym^{k−2} for weights 0, k−1.
Henniart's property of σ(τ) (R30.4/henniart-types): LL(V)|_K ⊇ σ(τ) because WD(V)|_I ≅ τ; hence σ(k, τ) ↪ Π(V)^{alg} ⊂ Π(V) = Θ ⊗ ℚ_p.
Abelian types: Berger–Breuil and Colmez give the completion directly (Kisin Theorem (1.2.8), R30.4/berger-breuil-completion).
acceptance: For τ trivial and k = 2, σ(2, 1) is the trivial K-representation and Θ ⊗ ℚ_p has a nonzero K-fixed vector.
The hypothesis holds for all de Rham V with abelian type unconditionally.

sources.locator: §1.1 and Hypothesis (1.2.6), Theorem (1.2.8), (1.2.7), pp. 4–9 of the author's preprint
sources.match: Defines type (k, τ, ψ) (potentially semistable of type τ, Hodge–Tate weights 0, k−1, determinant ψχ_cyc), states Hypothesis (1.2.6) asking for an admissible lattice with V(Θ) ⊗ ℚ_p = V and a K-equivariant σ(k, τ) ↪ Θ ⊗ ℚ_p, and proves it for τ of abelian type.
Identifies the locally algebraic vectors of B(V) for all de Rham V with distinct weights, which gives Kisin's hypothesis for every type.
Records that the compatibility between classical and p-adic local Langlands in Kisin's article is supplied by Emerton (lg Theorem 1.2.1) and Paškūnas (Duke 2015, Theorem 1.1).

nodes.title: Classification of unitary completions; weights do not determine Π
nodes.statement: Let π be an admissible absolutely irreducible infinite-dimensional smooth L-representation of G, W = Sym^{k−1}L² ⊗ det^a (k ≥ 1), Δ the Weil representation attached to π by the classical correspondence (viewed as a (φ, G_{ℚ_p})-module), and F(Δ, W) the set of weakly admissible absolutely irreducible filtered (φ, N, G_{ℚ_p})-modules with underlying Δ and filtration jumps −a, −a−k. (i) If Π is an admissible absolutely irreducible non-ordinary unitary completion of π ⊗ W then V(Π) is potentially semistable with Hodge–Tate weights a, a+k and D_pst(V(Π)) has underlying (φ, G_{ℚ_p})-module Δ. (ii) Π ↦ D_pst(V(Π)) is a bijection from such completions onto F(Δ, W), which is a point if π is a principal series and ℙ¹(L) if π is supercuspidal or a twist of the Steinberg. In particular St ⊗ |det|^{k/2} ⊗ Sym^k L² has exactly ℙ¹(L) pairwise non-isomorphic absolutely irreducible admissible unitary completions (Breuil's conjecture): a p-adic Banach representation is not determined by its Hodge–Tate weights and locally algebraic vectors.
hypotheses: π infinite-dimensional; completions absolutely irreducible, admissible, non-ordinary; the supercuspidal case uses Emerton's local-global compatibility (CDP footnote 5), i.e. gap G1.
proofSteps: Combine R30.3/cdp-correspondence (every such completion is Π(V)), R30.4/locally-algebraic-vectors (Π(V)^{alg} = LL(V) ⊗ Alg(V) and its independence of the filtration) and the converse that Π(D_ℒ) completes LL(M, a, b) for each ℒ ∈ F (Colmez Théorème VI.6.42, Remarque 0.22).
Distinct ℒ give non-isomorphic Π(D_ℒ) since V(Π(D_ℒ)) = V(D_ℒ) are non-isomorphic.
acceptance: For π = St ⊗ |det|^{k/2}, W = Sym^k: completions ↔ ℙ¹(L) (the L-invariant).
For π an irreducible principal series, the completion is unique.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.3 and the paragraph before it, p. 2
sources.match: Proves that admissible absolutely irreducible non-ordinary completions of π ⊗ W correspond bijectively to F(Δ, W), a point for principal series and ℙ¹(L) for supercuspidal or Steinberg π.
Deduces that St ⊗ |det|^{k/2} ⊗ Sym^k L² admits precisely ℙ¹(L) non-isomorphic absolutely irreducible admissible unitary completions, confirming Breuil's conjecture.

The filtrations with jumps a < b are parametrised by ℙ¹(M_dR) minus finitely many points and the Jordan–Hölder constituents of Π(D_ℒ)^{an} do not depend on ℒ; the filtration is encoded in the extension.

nodes.title: Kirillov models of P-algebraic and locally algebraic vectors
nodes.statement: Let D ∈ ΦΓ^et(E) be irreducible of rank 2, almost de Rham with Hodge–Tate weights ℓ < ℓ + k, Π = Π(D), and X^-_∞ ⊂ D̃_dif/D̃⁺_dif the L_∞[t]/t^k-module of Colmez §VI.4. (i) For z ∈ Π^{alg}, K_z(x) f_D = ι^-_0((x 0; 0 1)·z) defines K_z : ℚ_p^× → L_∞[t]/t^k with σ_a(K_z(x)) = K_z(ax), its coefficients locally constant with compact support in ℚ_p, and z ↦ K_z is a bijection of Π^{alg} onto its Kirillov model. (ii) Π^{alg}, if nonzero, is of type (ℓ, k) and irreducible, except in the special case where it is an extension of W_{ℓ,k} ⊗ (δ₀∘det) by W_{ℓ,k} ⊗ St ⊗ (δ₀∘det) for a smooth δ₀. (iii) The P-algebraic vectors with compact support Π^{P−alg}_c satisfy: z ↦ φ_z is a B-equivariant isomorphism Π^{P−alg}_c ≅ LP_c(ℚ_p^×, X^-_∞)^Γ (locally polynomial, compactly supported functions with Γ-equivariance), Π^{P−alg}_c ⊂ Π^{an}, and Π^{P−alg}_c ⊂ Π^{alg} when Π^{alg} ≠ 0. This is the P-equivariant embedding of functions on ℚ_p^× with values in D^-_dif into Π(V)^{la} used by consumers.
hypotheses: D irreducible of rank 2, almost de Rham with weights ℓ < ℓ + k (for (i)–(ii)); (iii) for D irreducible of rank 2 with these weights.
proofSteps: (i): Proposition VI.5.6 from Lemme VI.5.4 (the map z ↦ φ_z = ι^-_0 on the B-orbit).
(ii): Théorème VI.5.7, from the Kirillov model and Proposition VI.2.12 on smooth representations with a Kirillov model.
(iii): Proposition VI.5.8 (surjectivity via an explicit lift in Ñ_dif), Corollaire VI.5.9 and Proposition VI.5.12(i).
acceptance: For D crystalline irreducible with weights 0, k, the Kirillov functions of Π^{alg} take values in L_∞[t]/t^k and are compactly supported in ℚ_p.
Π^{P−alg}_c ≅ ⊕_{i∈ℤ} X^-_∞ via z ↦ (ι^-_i(z̃))_i (Lemme VI.5.10).

sources.locator: §VI.5.2–VI.5.4: Proposition VI.5.6 and Théorème VI.5.7, p. 167; Proposition VI.5.8, Corollaire VI.5.9 and Lemme VI.5.10, p. 168; Proposition VI.5.12(i), p. 169
sources.match: Constructs K_z with σ_a(K_z(x)) = K_z(ax) and shows z ↦ K_z is a bijection onto the Kirillov model; Π^{alg} is of type (ℓ, k), irreducible or the special Steinberg extension; z ↦ φ_z identifies the compactly supported P-algebraic vectors with LP_c(ℚ_p^×, X^-_∞)^Γ, inside Π^{an}.

nodes.title: Locally analytic vectors of the unitary principal series (trianguline case)
nodes.statement: Let s = (δ₁, δ₂, ℒ) ∈ S_irr (R30.1/trianguline-representation), Δ(s) the trianguline (φ,Γ)-module over R, and Π(Δ(s)) = Π(V(s))^{an}. For η₁, η₂ ∈ T̂(L) let Ban(η₁, η₂) := Ind^{an}_B^G(η₂ ⊗ η₁χ^{−1}) (locally analytic induction). (i) J*(Π(Δ)) ≠ 0 iff Δ is triangulable, i.e. iff Π(Δ̂[0]) is a unitary principal series. (ii) If s is generic (δ_s := χ^{−1}δ₁δ₂^{−1} ∉ {x^k : k ∈ ℕ}), there is an exact sequence 0 → Ban(δ₁, δ₂) → Π(Δ(s)) → Ban(δ₂, δ₁) → 0, and Π(Δ(s)) is the unique non-trivial such extension. (iii) If s is special, Ban(δ₁, δ₂) contains a (k+1)-dimensional subrepresentation W(δ₁, δ₂) with quotient St^{an}(δ₁, δ₂), Ext¹(R(δ₂), R(δ₁)) ≅ Ext¹(W(δ₁, δ₂), St^{an}(δ₁, δ₂)), and 0 → E_ℒ → Π(Δ(s)) → Ban(δ₂, δ₁) → 0 with E_ℒ the extension determined by ℒ; for δ_s = x^k these are Breuil's ℒ-invariant extensions. (iv) Π(V(s)) is the universal unitary completion of ker p_s.
hypotheses: s ∈ S_irr; p ≠ 2 where Colmez's trianguline classification is used (gap G2).
proofSteps: Compute the Jacquet-type module J*(s) of Π(Δ(s)) (Colmez 2014, Théorème 0.6) from the description of Π(D)^{an} through D_rig ⊠ ℙ¹ (R30.3/analytic-vectors-of-pi).
An eigenvector of B in J*(Π) gives a G-map to Ind^{an}; this gives p_s : Π(Δ(s)) → Ban(δ₂, δ₁), shown surjective with the stated kernel (Théorème 0.7).
Uniqueness of the extension: dim Ext¹(Ban(δ₂, δ₁), Ban(δ₁, δ₂)) = 1 for generic s (Remarque 0.8(i), citing Liu–Xie–Zhang); (iv) is Remarque 0.8(iii).
acceptance: For V crystalline irreducible with distinct eigenvalues, Π(V)^{an} is an extension of two locally analytic principal series.
For V semistable non-crystalline, the extension class of E_ℒ recovers the Fontaine–Mazur ℒ-invariant.

sources.locator: Théorème 0.1, p. 5; Propositions 0.2–0.5, pp. 5–6; Théorèmes 0.6–0.7 and Remarque 0.8, p. 7
sources.match: J*(Π(Δ)) ≠ 0 iff Δ is triangulable; for s ∈ S_irr the map p_s : Π(Δ(s)) → Ban(δ₂, δ₁) is onto with kernel Ban(δ₁, δ₂) in the generic case and Breuil's extension E_ℒ in the special case; Π(V(s)) is the universal completion of ker p_s.

nodes.title: Density of locally algebraic vectors and de Rham extensions (Dospinescu)
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 5 and Π ∈ Rep_L(δ) supersingular with Π^{alg} ≠ 0 (so Π = Π(V) with V de Rham with distinct weights). For an extension 0 → Π → Π₁ → Π → 0 in Rep_L(δ), the following are equivalent: (a) Π₁^{alg} is dense in Π₁; (b) Π₁^{alg} ≠ Π^{alg}; (c) V(Π₁) is de Rham. Consequently V induces an isomorphism Ext¹_{alg}(Π, Π) ≅ Ext¹_{g,ζ}(V(Π), V(Π)) onto the de Rham extensions with fixed determinant, and if Π ∈ Rep_L(δ) is the completion of its locally algebraic vectors then V(Π) is de Rham. The converse fails: V(Π) de Rham does not force Π to be the completion of Π^{alg}.
hypotheses: p ≥ 5; Π supersingular (all Jordan–Hölder factors of the reduction supersingular) with Π^{alg} ≠ 0; central character δ fixed.
proofSteps: Describe Π^{P−fin} as a dense B-stable subspace of Π^{an} (Dospinescu Théorème 1.8) and the P-algebraic compactly supported vectors (R30.4/kirillov-model).
Hodge–Tate case first (Théorème 1.9(a)–(b)), then the de Rham criterion via the inclusion Π₁^{P−alg}_c ⊂ Π₁^{alg} (Théorème 1.9(c)).
The Ext¹ isomorphism (Théorème 1.3) and the completion criterion (Théorème 1.7) follow.
acceptance: For Π₁ a non-de Rham self-extension, Π₁^{alg} = Π^{alg}.
The trivial extension Π ⊕ Π has V de Rham and dense locally algebraic vectors.

sources.locator: Théorèmes 1.2 and 1.3, pp. 3–4; Théorème 1.7 and Remarque 1.1, pp. 2–6; Théorèmes 1.8–1.9, p. 7

nodes.title: Blocks of locally finite mod p representations
nodes.statement: On the set of isomorphism classes of irreducible objects of Mod^{l.fin}_{G,ζ}(O) (equivalently of Rep^{ℓf}G with central character ζ) put τ ∼ π if there is a chain τ = τ₀, τ₁, …, τ_n = π of irreducibles with τ_i ≅ τ_{i+1} or Ext¹_G(τ_i, τ_{i+1}) ≠ 0 or Ext¹_G(τ_{i+1}, τ_i) ≠ 0. An equivalence class B is a block, Mod^{l.fin}_{G,ζ}(O)_B the full subcategory of objects all of whose irreducible subquotients lie in B, π_B = ⊕_{π∈B} π, J_B an injective envelope of π_B, P_B = J_B^∨ (a projective envelope of π_B^∨ in C_{G,ζ}(O)), Ẽ_B = End_G(J_B) ≅ End_{C(O)}(P_B)^{op} with its pseudo-compact topology, and Z_B its centre, which is the centre of the category Mod^{l.fin}_{G,ζ}(O)_B. Gabriel: Mod^{l.fin}_{G,ζ}(O) ≅ ∏_B Mod^{l.fin}_{G,ζ}(O)_B, and τ ↦ m_B(τ) := Hom_G(τ, J_B) (equivalently Hom_{C(O)}(P_B, τ^∨)) is an anti-equivalence of Mod^{l.fin}_{G,ζ}(O)_B with compact Ẽ_B-modules, with Π ≅ ⊕_B (m_B(Π) ⊗_{Ẽ_B} P_B)^∨ for finite length Π. Blocks over k_L are Gal(𝔽̄_p/k_L)-orbits of blocks over 𝔽̄_p.
hypotheses: ζ fixed; F = ℚ_p; blocks may be taken over k_L or 𝔽̄_p (rationality as in CDN 2023 Remarques 1.11 and 1.13).
proofSteps: Mod^{l.fin}_{G,ζ}(O) is a locally finite Grothendieck category (R30.2/smooth-torsion-categories); Gabriel's decomposition of locally finite categories into blocks applies (Paškūnas 2013 §1.1 and [35, §IV] there).
The anti-equivalence with compact Ẽ_B-modules is Gabriel's theorem for categories with a projective generator in the dual (R30.2/pontryagin-dual-category).
Rationality: Lemma 1.6 and Lemma 1.7 of CDN 2023 (Hom and absolute irreducibility under field extension) give the Galois-orbit description.
acceptance: A supersingular π alone forms a block {π}.
The centre Z_B acts on every object of the block, functorially.

nodes.title: Paškūnas's classification of blocks and the bijection B ↔ ρ̄_B
nodes.statement: The blocks of Rep_{𝔽̄_p}G containing an absolutely irreducible representation are: (i) {π}, π supersingular; (ii) {Ind_B^G(δ₁ ⊗ δ₂ω^{−1}), Ind_B^G(δ₂ ⊗ δ₁ω^{−1})} with δ₂δ₁^{−1} ∉ {1, ω^{±1}}; (iii) for p > 2, {Ind_B^G(δ ⊗ δω^{−1})}; (iv) for p = 2, {1, Sp} ⊗ δ∘det; (v) for p ≥ 5, {1, Sp, Ind_B^G(ω ⊗ ω^{−1})} ⊗ δ∘det; (vi) for p = 3, {1, Sp, ω∘det, Sp ⊗ ω∘det} ⊗ δ∘det (δ, δ₁, δ₂ smooth characters, ω(x) = x|x| mod ϖ). There is a bijection B ↦ ρ̄_B between blocks over 𝔽̄_p and semisimple two-dimensional 𝔽̄_p-representations of G_{ℚ_p}, sending B to the semisimple representation whose irreducible constituents are the V(π), π ∈ B (up to the twist normalising V): ρ̄_B irreducible for (i), δ₁ ⊕ δ₂ for (ii), δ ⊕ δ for (iii), δ ⊕ δω for (iv)–(vi); in all cases (det ρ̄_B)ε^{−1} is the central character of B. Over k_L blocks correspond to Gal(𝔽̄_p/k_L)-orbits, and with central character δ to ρ̄ with det = δε.
hypotheses: F = ℚ_p; the exceptional cases at p = 2, 3 as listed.
