nodes.title: Projective envelopes P̃ and Paškūnas's axiomatic framework
nodes.statement: Let π be an irreducible object of Mod^{l.fin}_{G,ζ}(O) with End_G(π) = k, S = π^∨, and P̃ ↠ S a projective envelope in C(O) (R30.2/pontryagin-dual-category); Ẽ := End_{C(O)}(P̃) is a local, pseudo-compact (hence compact, k being finite) ring with residue field k. Suppose Q ∈ C(k) of finite length satisfies (H1) Hom_{C(k)}(Q, S') = 0 for irreducible S' ≇ S; (H2) S occurs in Q with multiplicity 1; (H3) Ext¹_{C(k)}(Q, S') = 0 for S' ≇ S; (H4) Ext¹_{C(k)}(Q, S) finite-dimensional; (H5) Ext²_{C(k)}(Q, rad Q) = 0; (H0) Hom_{C(k)}(P̃[ϖ], rad Q) = 0. Then the natural topology on Ẽ is the 𝔪-adic one, P̃ is flat over Ẽ and k ⊗̂_{Ẽ} P̃ ≅ Q; the functor M ↦ Hom_{C(O)}(P̃, M) relates C(O) to compact Ẽ-modules, and V̌(P̃) carries a natural action of Ẽ (R30.3/montreal-functor). For a block, P_B = ⊕_{π∈B} P̃_π.
hypotheses: π irreducible with End = k (after enlarging k); hypotheses (H0)–(H5) for the flatness statements.
proofSteps: Existence of projective envelopes: duals of injective envelopes (R30.2/pontryagin-dual-category).
Locality and pseudo-compactness of Ẽ: Paškūnas 2013 §2.
Under (H0)–(H5): Proposition 3.8 and its corollaries (Proposition 1.12 in the introduction) prove the coincidence of topologies, flatness and k ⊗̂ P̃ ≅ Q.
acceptance: For G pro-p and π trivial (Paškūnas's example), Ẽ is the completed group algebra.
P̃ is not of finite length.

sources.match: Sets up P̃ ↠ S in C(O), shows Ẽ = End(P̃) is local and compact, states hypotheses (H0)–(H5) on a finite length Q and proves the topology on Ẽ is 𝔪-adic, P̃ flat over Ẽ and k ⊗̂_Ẽ P̃ ≅ Q.

nodes.title: The pseudodeformation ring R^{ps,δ}_B of a block
nodes.statement: For a block B with semisimple ρ̄_B (R30.5/blocks-classification) and a continuous character δ lifting the central character, R^{ps,δ}_B := R^{ps,δε}_{tr ρ̄_B} is the complete local noetherian O-algebra pro-representing deformations of the two-dimensional pseudocharacter tr ρ̄_B of G_{ℚ_p} with determinant δε, with universal pseudocharacter T^δ_B : G_{ℚ_p} → R^{ps,δ}_B. It is the universal pseudocharacter ring of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.1 for GL₂, completed at tr ρ̄_B and cut out by the determinant condition; for p = 2 Chenevier's determinants replace pseudocharacters (IHG.0). R^{ps,δ}_B[[G_{ℚ_p}]]/J denotes the largest Cayley–Hamilton quotient.
hypotheses: G_{ℚ_p} satisfies Mazur's finiteness condition Φ_p; for p = 2 use determinants (IHG.0/determinant-trace-bijective-small does not apply).
proofSteps: Universal pseudocharacter rings: IHG.1/universal-reductive-pseudocharacter-ring for H = GL₂, completed at the residual pseudocharacter (noetherian by Chenevier, since G_{ℚ_p} satisfies Φ_p).
The determinant condition: impose det = δε via the determinant of the pseudocharacter (a quotient by a closed ideal).
For p > 2, pseudocharacters and determinants agree (IHG.0/determinant-trace-bijective-small with d = 2 and 2 invertible).

nodes.title: Paškūnas: endomorphism rings of projective envelopes are deformation rings
nodes.statement: Assume p ≥ 5 (and for (iii) p = 2 with B of type (i) or (ii)). (i) For every block B, the centre of Ẽ_B, hence of Mod^{l.fin}_{G,ζ}(O)_B, is naturally isomorphic to R^{ps,ζε}_{tr ρ̄_B}; Ẽ_B is finitely generated over its centre and is a matrix algebra over it after localising away from the reducible locus. (ii) If B = {π} with π supersingular, V(J_B)^∨(ζε) ≅ ρ^{un} and Ẽ_B ≅ R^{ζε}_ρ, ρ = V(π); if B is of type (ii), V(J_B)^∨(ζε) ≅ ρ₁^{un} ⊕ ρ₂^{un} and Ẽ_B ≅ End_{G_{ℚ_p}}(ρ₁^{un} ⊕ ρ₂^{un}), ρ₁, ρ₂ the non-split extensions. (iii) (p = 2, Paškūnas 2016) for B of types (i), (ii) the centre of Mod^{l.adm}_{G,ψ}(O)[B] is R^{ps,ψ} and, for B = {π}, E_B is the fixed-determinant deformation ring of ρ̄^{ss}. (iv) Ban^{adm}_{G,ζ}(L) = ⊕_B Ban^{adm}_{G,ζ}(L)_B; for B containing an absolutely irreducible object, Ban^{adm.fl}_{G,ζ}(L)_B ≅ ⊕_{𝔫 ∈ MaxSpec R^{ps}[1/p]} Ban^{adm.fl}_{G,ζ}(L)_{B,𝔫}, the 𝔫-part anti-equivalent to finite length modules over the 𝔫-adic completion of Ẽ_B[1/p]; when T_𝔫 is the trace of an absolutely irreducible V this is finite length modules over the completion of R^{ps}[1/p], with the unique irreducible Π_𝔫 the non-ordinary Π with V(Π_𝔫) ≅ V; when T_𝔫 = ψ₁ + ψ₂, the irreducibles are subquotients of the two unitary principal series. (v) For Π absolutely irreducible non-ordinary with V = V(Π), Ban^{adm.fl}_{G,ζ}(L)_Π is a direct summand equivalent to finite length R^{ζε}_V-modules via B ↦ Hom(V^u, V̌(B)).
hypotheses: p ≥ 5 for (i), (ii), (iv), (v) (Paškūnas 2013); p = 2 and blocks (i), (ii) for (iii) (Paškūnas 2016); the remaining primes and blocks are covered by R30.5/local-r-equals-t.
proofSteps: Verify (H0)–(H5) for Q built from π (R30.5/projective-envelope) by Ext computations in the block (Paškūnas 2013 §§6–10), giving Ẽ local with 𝔪-adic topology.
V̌ gives Ẽ → R^{ζε}_ρ (or End of the universal deformations) for the generic blocks; it is an isomorphism by comparing graded rings (§§6, 8).
Non-generic blocks: Cayley–Hamilton quotients and the centre (§§9–10).
Banach representations: §§4, 11 and Proposition 1.8, Corollary 1.9, Theorems 1.10–1.11 by the Chinese remainder theorem over MaxSpec R^{ps}[1/p].
acceptance: For B = {π} supersingular and p ≥ 5, Ẽ_B ≅ R^{ζε}_ρ is commutative.
For generic reducible B, Ẽ_B is not commutative but its centre is R^{ps}.

For p = 2 and blocks of types (i), (ii): E_B is the fixed-determinant deformation ring of ρ̄^{ss} for supersingular blocks, the centre is R^{ps,ψ}, and V̌ gives the bijection with Galois representations.

nodes.title: The local R = T theorem for every block (Paškūnas–Tung)
nodes.statement: For every p and every block B with central character ζ (over k after enlarging it): (i) there is an O-algebra map υ : R^{ps,ζε}_{tr ρ̄_B} → Z_B such that for all τ ∈ Mod^{l.fin}_{G,ζ}(O)_B and g ∈ G_{ℚ_p}, V̌(c_τ(υ(T(g)))) = ρ_{V̌(τ^∨)}(g) + ρ_{V̌(τ^∨)}(g^{−1})ζε(g) in End^{cont}_{G_{ℚ_p}}(V̌(τ^∨)); equivalently (CDN) the unique ι^δ_B : R^{ps,δ}_B → Z^δ_B with ι^δ_B(T^δ_B(g)) = g + δε(g)g^{−1} in End(V(π)) for all π ∈ B. (ii) Z_B and E_B are finitely generated R^{ps}-modules; Z_B is noetherian, complete local with residue field k, O-torsion free with Z_B[1/p] normal. (iii) υ[1/p] : R^{ps}[1/p] ≅ Z_B[1/p]; if p ≥ 5, ι^δ_B is an isomorphism; if p = 3, Z_B = R^{ps}/(O-torsion); if p = 2, the cokernel of R^{ps}/(O-torsion) → Z_B is killed by 2. (iv) The essential image of Mod^{l.fin}_{G,ζ}(O)_B under V̌ is anti-equivalent to pseudo-compact (R^{ps}[[G_{ℚ_p}]]/J)_{tf}-modules.
hypotheses: All p; B any block (after a finite extension of k).
proofSteps: Construct υ (the main point of Paškūnas–Tung, by a new argument covering the exceptional blocks) using V̌ of P_B and Cayley–Hamilton algebras.
Finiteness (Theorem 1.3) by bounding E_B over R^{ps}, using Chenevier's noetherianity of R^{ps}.
Isomorphism after inverting p and the p = 2, 3 defects (Theorem 1.4); Corollary 1.5 for the properties of Z_B.
CDN 2023 Théorème 1.16 restates (i)–(iii) with the explicit identity ι^δ_B(T^δ_B(g)) = g + δε(g)g^{−1}.
acceptance: For B = {π} supersingular and p ≥ 5, ι^δ_B is the isomorphism R^{ζε}_ρ ≅ Ẽ_B of R30.5/paskunas-endomorphism-rings.
At p = 2 the map R^{ps} → Z_B need not be surjective; its cokernel is 2-torsion.

sources.match: Constructs υ : R^{ps,ζε}_{tr ρ̄} → Z_B compatible with V̌, proves Z_B and E_B finite over R^{ps}, R^{ps}[1/p] ≅ Z_B[1/p], Z_B = R^{ps}_{tf} for p ≠ 2 with a 2-torsion cokernel for p = 2, and describes the essential image of V̌.
The unique ι^δ_B : R^{ps,δ}_B → Z^δ_B with ι^δ_B(T^δ_B(g)) = g + δε(g)g^{−1} in End(V(π)): an isomorphism for p ≥ 5, after inverting p in general, with the p = 3 and p = 2 statements.

nodes.title: Kisin: deformations of π̄ and of ρ̄ coincide
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_{ℚ_p} → GL₂(𝔽) satisfy ρ̄ ≇ χ ⊗ (1 *; 0 ε) for every character χ. (i) (Colmez) There is a finite length object π̄ of Mod^{adm}_G(𝔽), unique up to isomorphism, with MF(π̄) ≅ ρ̄, central character det(ρ̄)ε, and no finite-dimensional subquotient. (ii) (Kisin) If moreover p ≥ 3 and End_{𝔽[G_{ℚ_p}]}(ρ̄) = 𝔽, the deformation functors Def(π̄) (orthonormalizable admissible deformations to complete local O-algebras) and Def(ρ̄) are representable and MF : Def(π̄) → Def(ρ̄) is an isomorphism; on a deformation π the centre acts through det(MF(π))ε; the same holds with fixed central character ψ and fixed determinant ψε^{−1}. (iii) (Emerton) Under (i) only, MF induces a fully faithful embedding Def*(π̄) ↪ Def(ρ̄), an equivalence on the crystabelline loci Def^{crys}.
hypotheses: ρ̄ not a twist of a non-split extension of ε by 1 in the stated direction; (ii) needs p ≥ 3 and End(ρ̄) = 𝔽.
proofSteps: (i): Colmez's construction of atoms and Emerton's Theorem 3.3.2.

(ii): injectivity on tangent spaces Ext¹(π̄, π̄) → Ext¹(ρ̄, ρ̄) (R30.3/ext1-injectivity) gives a closed immersion of deformation spaces; the image contains the Zariski-dense trianguline (crystabelline) points (R30.1/trianguline-representation), hence equality.
(iii): Emerton Theorem 3.3.13.
acceptance: For ρ̄ absolutely irreducible, π̄ is the supersingular π with V(π) ≅ ρ̄(ε) normalisations as in R30.3/montreal-functor, and Def(π̄) ≅ Def(ρ̄).

sources.locator: Assumption 3.3.1 and Theorem 3.3.2, p. 24; Definitions 3.3.6–3.3.11 and Theorem 3.3.13, pp. 25–26
sources.match: For ρ̄ not of the form χ ⊗ (1 *; 0 ε) there is a unique finite length π̄ with MF(π̄) ≅ ρ̄, central character det(ρ̄)ε and no finite-dimensional subobject or quotient; MF gives a fully faithful Def*(π̄) ↪ Def(ρ̄), an equivalence on crystabelline loci.

sources.locator: Theorem B.18, Definition B.19, Theorem B.20, Remark B.21, Definition B.22, pp. 98–99 (arXiv)
sources.match: Restates Colmez's π̄ and Kisin's theorem that MF : Def(π̄) → Def(ρ̄) is an isomorphism for p ≥ 3 and End(ρ̄) = 𝔽, with the centre acting by det(MF(π))ε, and the fixed-determinant variants.

nodes.title: P̃ is the dual of the universal deformation of π̄
nodes.statement: Assume p ≥ 5, End(ρ̄) = 𝔽, ρ̄ ≇ χ ⊗ (ε *; 0 1) and ρ̄ ≇ χ ⊗ (1 *; 0 ε). Let π̄ be as in R30.5/kisin-deformation-comparison, π_{π̄} its universal deformation over R_ρ̄ (and π^ψ_{π̄} with central character ψ over R^{ψε^{−1}}_ρ̄), and P̃^ψ, P̃ the projective envelopes of the dual of the socle in C^ψ(O), C(O). (i) For A ∈ Comp(O) and a deformation π with central character ψ, the A-dual π* lies in C^ψ(O) and V̌(π*) ≅ MF(π)(ε). (ii) (Paškūnas) V̌ induces End_{C^ψ(O)}(P̃^ψ) ≅ R^{ψε}_{ρ̄(ε)}, P̃^ψ is flat over it and V̌(P̃^ψ) is the universal deformation. (iii) There are G-equivariant topological isomorphisms P̃^ψ ≅ (π^ψ_{π̄})*, R^{ψε^{−1}}_ρ̄-linear, and P̃ ≅ π*_{π̄}, R_ρ̄-linear; with R_ρ̄ ≅ R^{ψε^{−1}}_ρ̄ ⊗̂ Λ and P̃ ≅ P̃^ψ ⊗̂ (1^{univ}∘det^{−1}), R_ρ̄ ≅ End_{C(O)}(P̃).
hypotheses: p ≥ 5; End(ρ̄) = 𝔽; ρ̄ not a twist of (ε *; 0 1) nor of (1 *; 0 ε).
proofSteps: (i): Lemma B.23, from the definition of V̌ and Pontryagin duality.
(ii): Theorem B.24, quoting Paškūnas 2013 (R30.5/paskunas-endomorphism-rings).

(iii): Lemma B.25 and Proposition B.26: compare the universal properties of P̃^ψ (projectivity, Hom(P̃^ψ, −) on the dual category) and of π^ψ_{π̄} through Kisin's isomorphism Def(π̄) ≅ Def(ρ̄); twist away the central character with the universal character of the centre (CEGGPS Theorem 6.18 as quoted).
acceptance: The reduction of P̃ modulo 𝔪_{R_ρ̄} is π̄^∨.

sources.locator: Lemma B.23, Theorem B.24, Lemma B.25, Proposition B.26, pp. 100–103 (arXiv)
sources.match: The dual of a deformation lies in C^ψ(O) with V̌(π*) ≅ MF(π)(ε); End(P̃^ψ) ≅ R^{ψε}_{ρ̄(ε)} under p ≥ 5, End(ρ̄) = 𝔽 and ρ̄ ≇ χ ⊗ (ε *; 0 1); P̃^ψ ≅ (π^ψ_{π̄})* and P̃ ≅ π*_{π̄} as G-equivariant topological isomorphisms.

nodes.title: Removing P̃ from Hom
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of R30.5/dual-of-universal-deformation, for every compact R_ρ̄-module M the map M → Hom_{C(O)}(P̃, P̃ ⊗̂_{R_ρ̄} M), m ↦ (v ↦ v ⊗̂ m), is a topological R_ρ̄-linear isomorphism; consequently, for compact R_ρ̄-modules M₁, M₂, f ↦ id_{P̃} ⊗ f is an R_ρ̄-linear isomorphism Hom^{cont}_{R_ρ̄}(M₁, M₂) ≅ Hom^{cont}_{R_ρ̄[G]}(P̃ ⊗̂ M₁, P̃ ⊗̂ M₂).
hypotheses: As in R30.5/dual-of-universal-deformation.
proofSteps: P̃ is projective in C(O) and flat over R_ρ̄ = End(P̃) (R30.5/dual-of-universal-deformation, R30.5/projective-envelope); Hom(P̃, P̃ ⊗̂ M) commutes with inverse limits of finite length M and equals End(P̃) ⊗̂ M = M (Lemma B.27).
Corollary B.28 follows by applying Lemma B.27 to M₂ and composing.
acceptance: For M = R_ρ̄ this recovers End(P̃) = R_ρ̄.

sources.locator: Lemma B.27 and Corollary B.28, p. 104 (arXiv)
sources.match: For compact R_ρ̄-modules M the map M → Hom_{C(O)}(P̃, P̃ ⊗̂ M) is a topological isomorphism, and f ↦ id ⊗ f identifies Hom_{R_ρ̄} with Hom_{R_ρ̄[G]} of the completed tensor products.

nodes.title: The Breuil–Mézard cycle identity for ρ̄
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_{ℚ_p} → GL₂(k), R^□ = R^□_ρ̄ its framed deformation ring (LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.1) and R^{□,ψ} the fixed-determinant quotient (det = ψε). For a p-adic Hodge type (w, τ, ψ), w = (a, b) with b > a and ψ|_{I} = ε^{a+b}det τ (Paškūnas's normalisation; Kisin and Tung use det = ψε with ψ|_I = ε^{k−2}det τ), let R^{□,ψ}(w, τ) and R^{□,ψ,cr}(w, τ) be Kisin's reduced O-flat potentially semistable (resp. crystalline) quotients (LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.3/pst-deformation-ring), of relative dimension 4 when nonzero (2 for the unframed version when End ρ̄ = k). For a noetherian R and d, Z_d(R) is the free abelian group on primes 𝔭 with dim R/𝔭 = d and z_d(M) = Σ ℓ_{R_𝔭}(M_𝔭)[𝔭] (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.6/cycle-specialization-multiplicity). ρ̄ satisfies the Breuil–Mézard cycle identity if there are cycles C_σ(ρ̄) ∈ Z_4(R^{□,ψ}/ϖ) (resp. z(σ, ρ̄) ∈ Z_1(R^ψ_ρ̄/ϖ) unframed), one for each irreducible smooth k-representation σ of K, independent of (w, τ), with z_4(R^{□,ψ}(w, τ)/ϖ) = Σ_σ m_σ(w, τ)C_σ(ρ̄) and z_4(R^{□,ψ,cr}(w, τ)/ϖ) = Σ_σ m^cr_σ(w, τ)C_σ(ρ̄), the multiplicities m_σ, m^cr_σ being those of R30.4/henniart-types. The numerical version replaces cycles by Hilbert–Samuel multiplicities e(R^{□,ψ}(w, τ)/ϖ) = Σ_σ m_σ(w, τ)μ_σ(ρ̄).
hypotheses: ρ̄ continuous; L large enough; framed or (when End ρ̄ = k) unframed rings, with the determinant normalisation of the source fixed explicitly.
proofSteps: The rings R^{□,ψ}(w, τ) exist with the stated dimensions by Kisin (LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.3/pst-deformation-ring and pst-generic-fibre).

Cycles and multiplicities: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.6 (z_d and specialization) and key/hilbert-samuel-multiplicity; the cycle identity implies the numerical one by taking multiplicities.
Independence of (w, τ) is part of the definition: the C_σ depend only on ρ̄ and σ.
acceptance: For w = (0, 1) and τ trivial, the crystalline identity reads z_4(R^{□,ψ,cr}(0,1; 1)/ϖ) = C_{triv}(ρ̄).
If no Serre weight σ of ρ̄ occurs in σ̄(w, τ), the identity forces R^{□,ψ}(w, τ) = 0.

sources.locator: §1, pp. 2–3: the p-adic Hodge type, Henniart's σ(τ), the cycle groups z_d and Theorem 1.1
sources.match: Fixes p-adic Hodge types (w, τ, ψ) with ψ|_I = ε^{a+b}det τ, the multiplicities m_σ(w, τ), the cycles z_d(M) = Σ ℓ(M_𝔭)𝔭, and states the cycle identity z₁(R^ψ_ρ̄(w, τ)/ϖ) = Σ m_σ(w, τ)z(σ, ρ̄).
States the numerical Breuil–Mézard conjecture e(R^{□,ψ}_r̄(λ, τ)/ϖ) = Σ m_σ̄(λ, τ)μ_σ̄(r̄) and its cycle version with 4-dimensional cycles C_σ̄(r̄), with det r = ψε and ψ|_I = ε^{a+b−1}det τ.

nodes.title: Paškūnas's criterion: supports of M(Θ) and the cycle formula
nodes.statement: Let N be a projective object in Mod^{pro}_K(O) with a compatible action of a complete local noetherian O-algebra R (R30.5/projective-envelope, e.g. N = P̃ with R = Ẽ_B or R^ψ_ρ̄), V a continuous representation of K on a finite-dimensional L-space with K-stable lattice Θ, M(Θ) := Hom^{cont}_{O[[K]]}(N, Θ^d)^d, 𝔞 its R-annihilator, d = dim R/𝔞, and for 𝔫 ∈ m-Spec R[1/p], Π(κ(𝔫)) the Banach representation attached to 𝔫. If (a) N is projective in Mod^{pro}_K(O); (b) R/𝔞 is equidimensional with all associated primes minimal; (c) there is a dense subset Σ ⊂ Supp M(Θ) ∩ m-Spec R[1/p] with dim Hom_K(V, Π(κ(𝔫))) = 1 and dim Hom_K(V, Π(R_𝔫/𝔫²)) ≤ d for 𝔫 ∈ Σ, then R/𝔞 is reduced of dimension d and z_{d−1}(R/(ϖ, 𝔞)) = Σ_σ m_σ z_{d−1}(M(σ)), m_σ the multiplicity of σ in Θ/ϖ. Applied to N = P̃ (p ≥ 5, End ρ̄ = k): for V = σ(w, τ) or σ^cr(w, τ), dim Hom_K(V, Π(κ(𝔫))) ≤ 1 with equality iff ρ^{un}_𝔫 is potentially semistable (resp. crystalline) of type (w, τ, ψ) (Proposition 4.14), so R^ψ_ρ̄/Ann M(Θ) = R^ψ_ρ̄(w, τ) (resp. the crystalline quotient) (Corollary 6.5); M^cr(k, τ) is locally free of rank one over R^cr(k, τ)[1/p] and M^st(k, τ) over the complement of the crystalline locus (Nakamura Theorem 4.7).
hypotheses: (a)–(c) as stated; for the application p ≥ 5, End ρ̄ = k and ρ̄ ≇ (ε *; 0 1) ⊗ η for the local freeness.
proofSteps: Paškūnas 2015 Theorem 2.42: projectivity of N gives exactness of Θ ↦ M(Θ); (b)–(c) control the generic rank along Σ, giving reducedness and the cycle formula by specialisation (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.6/cycle-specialization-multiplicity).

Proposition 4.14: by R30.4/kisin-hypothesis and R30.4/locally-algebraic-vectors, Hom_K(σ(w, τ), Π(V)) ≠ 0 iff V is potentially semistable of type (w, τ) (Henniart's property, R30.4/henniart-types), with multiplicity one.
Corollary 6.5 and Theorem 6.6 assemble these with R30.5/paskunas-endomorphism-rings.
acceptance: For σ irreducible with Hom_K(σ, π) ≠ 0, the Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity of M(σ) is 1 (Theorem 6.6).

sources.locator: Theorem 2.42, p. 16; Proposition 4.14, p. 23; Corollary 6.5 and Theorem 6.6, p. 31
sources.match: Under projectivity of N, equidimensionality and the multiplicity-one condition on a dense set, R/𝔞 is reduced of dimension d with the cycle formula; for V = σ(w, τ) the multiplicity condition holds exactly on the potentially semistable locus; hence R^ψ_ρ̄/Ann M(Θ) = R^ψ_ρ̄(w, τ) and the cycle identity with multiplicity-one M(σ).

For p ≥ 5, End ρ̄_p = 𝔽 and ρ̄_p ≇ (ε *; 0 1) ⊗ η: R_p/Ann(M^⋄_0(k, τ)) = R^⋄_p(k, τ) for ⋄ ∈ {st, cr}, with M^cr locally free of rank one over R^cr[1/p] and M^st locally free of rank one off the crystalline locus.

nodes.title: Kisin rings from the classical correspondence (Colmez–Dospinescu–Nizioł)
nodes.statement: Let M be an irreducible (φ, N, G_{ℚ_p})-module of rank 2, a < b integers with LL^{[a,b]}(M) := LL(M) ⊗ Sym^{b−a−1} ⊗ det^a having unitary central character, Λ a G-stable O_L-lattice in it, and B the block of finite length smooth representations determined by a semisimple ρ̄ : G_{ℚ_p} → GL₂(k_L). The B-adic completion Λ_B is the inverse limit of the finite length quotients of Λ all of whose Jordan–Hölder factors lie in B, LL^{[a,b]}_B(M) := L ⊗ Λ_B (independent of Λ), R^{[a,b]}_{M,B} := End_G(LL^{[a,b]}_B(M)) and ρ^{[a,b]}_M := V(LL^{[a,b]}_B(M)). Theorem (CDN, Théorème 0.1): R^{[a,b]}_{M,ρ̄} is commutative, the ring of bounded analytic functions on an analytic open of ℙ¹, algebraically a finite product of principal ideal domains; ρ^{[a,b]}_M is free of rank 2 over it and specialisation x ↦ ρ_x is a bijection between its L'-points and the L'-representations of G_{ℚ_p} with reduction ρ̄ and type (M, a, b) (potentially semistable with Hodge–Tate weights a, b and D_pst ≅ M). This is the GL₂(ℚ_p)-side construction of the rings R_{B,M} planned in LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.3/weil-deligne-type-ring.
hypotheses: M irreducible (so LL(M) supercuspidal); unitary central character; the hidden global ingredient of R30.4/locally-algebraic-vectors (v), i.e. gap G1, through the identification of M with LL(M).
proofSteps: Construct Λ_B and LL^{[a,b]}_B(M) by B-adic completion (CDN-Kisin §2).
Local R = T (R30.5/local-r-equals-t) shows V(LL_B) is of GL₂ type and gives the R^{ps}-action.

The de Rham extension criterion (R30.4/de-rham-extensions, extended) shows R^{[a,b]}_{M,B} is smooth and a product of principal ideal domains; the identification with bounded analytic functions on an open of ℙ¹ (§§3–5).
Comparison with Kisin's rings via the universal property of potentially semistable deformation rings (LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.3).
acceptance: For ρ̄ generic, the result is compatible with Kisin's rings, up to the ambiguity M versus M ⊗ μ_{−1} (CDN Remarque 0.2(i)).

sources.locator: Introduction, pp. 1–3: the construction, Théorème 0.1 and Remarque 0.2
sources.match: Defines the B-adic completion of a lattice in LL^{[a,b]}(M), the ring R^{[a,b]}_{M,ρ} = End_G(LL^{[a,b]}_B(M)) and ρ^{[a,b]}_M = V(LL^{[a,b]}_B(M)), and proves they are the universal family of representations of type (M, a, b) with reduction ρ, R being bounded analytic functions on an open of ℙ¹ and a finite product of PIDs; Remarque 0.2(v) notes the hidden global input.

nodes.title: Admittance of residual representations by types (BCDT)
nodes.statement: Let ℓ be a prime and ρ̄ : G_ℓ → GL₂(𝔽̄_ℓ) continuous. For the irreducible 𝔽̄_ℓ-representations σ_{n,m} of GL₂(ℤ_ℓ), σ'_{m₁,m₂} of U₀(ℓ) and σ'_{{m₁,m₂},a}, σ'_{{m},a} of Ũ₀(ℓ) (R30.2/mod-l-compact-irreducibles), Breuil–Conrad–Diamond–Taylor define when σ admits and simply admits ρ̄, explicitly in terms of ρ̄|_{I_ℓ} through the fundamental characters ω, ω₂, the peu/très ramifié condition, and central characters (ω^{−1}det ρ̄)|_{W_ℓ}; e.g. σ_{n,m} admits ρ̄ iff ρ̄|_{I_ℓ} ≅ ω₂^{1−ℓn−m(ℓ+1)} ⊕ ω₂^{ℓ−n−m(ℓ+1)} or ρ̄|_{I_ℓ} ≅ (ω^{1−m} *; 0 ω^{−n−m}) (peu ramifié if n = 0), and σ_{n,0} admits ρ̄ iff the Serre weight of ρ̄^∨ ⊗ ω is n + 2. An ℓ-type τ (reducible: σ_τ a representation of GL₂(ℤ_ℓ); irreducible: of U₀(ℓ); extended type τ' with irreducible restriction to I_ℓ: of Ũ₀(ℓ)) admits σ if σ is a Jordan–Hölder constituent of Λ ⊗ 𝔽̄_ℓ for an invariant lattice Λ ⊂ σ_τ, simply if with multiplicity one; τ (simply) admits ρ̄ if it admits some σ that admits ρ̄ (resp. a unique such σ, simply, which simply admits ρ̄).
hypotheses: Weight 2 (potentially Barsotti–Tate) types as in BCDT; the definition uses ρ̄ rather than its Cartier dual because of the normalisations of CDT.
proofSteps: Spell out each case of BCDT §1.3 on the classification of R30.2/mod-l-compact-irreducibles.
Relate σ_{n,0} admitting ρ̄ to Serre's weight of ρ̄^∨ ⊗ ω (BCDT's parenthetical remark).
acceptance: σ_{0,0} admits ρ̄ iff ρ̄|_{I_ℓ} ≅ (ω *; 0 1) peu ramifié or ρ̄|_{I_ℓ} ≅ ω₂ ⊕ ω₂^ℓ.
Simple admittance implies admittance.

nodes.title: BCDT's Conjecture 1.3.1(1) from the Breuil–Mézard identity
nodes.statement: Let p = ℓ, k ⊂ 𝔽̄_p finite, ρ̄ : G_{ℚ_p} → GL₂(k) continuous with centraliser k, τ an ℓ-type (resp. τ' an extended type with irreducible restriction to inertia) with tamely ramified determinant and non-central image. If ρ̄ satisfies the Breuil–Mézard cycle identity (R30.5/breuil-mezard-cycles) and C_σ(ρ̄) ≠ 0 exactly when σ is a Serre weight of ρ̄ in BCDT's sense (σ admits ρ̄), then τ (resp. τ') admits ρ̄ iff R^D_{V,O} ≠ 0 (resp. R^{D'}_{V,O} ≠ 0), i.e. iff ρ̄ has a potentially Barsotti–Tate lift of type τ (resp. extended type τ'). The identity holds for every ρ̄ when p > 2 (R30.6/tung-bm-p-odd) and when p = 2 (R30.6/tung-bm-p-two); Paškūnas 2015 gives C_σ(ρ̄) ≠ 0 iff Hom_K(σ, β) ≠ 0 for Colmez's atom β of ρ̄ when p ≥ 5 and End ρ̄ = k. Part (2) of the conjecture (simple admittance ⇔ acceptability) is not derived here: BCDT's 'acceptable' is a patching-theoretic condition, not a property of R^D alone.
hypotheses: p = ℓ; the hypotheses of BCDT Conjecture 1.3.1; the identification of {σ : C_σ(ρ̄) ≠ 0} with BCDT's admitted weights (gap G3).
proofSteps: For U₀(ℓ)- and Ũ₀(ℓ)-types induce σ_τ to GL₂(ℤ_ℓ): σ' admits ρ̄ iff a constituent of Ind σ' admits ρ̄ (BCDT §1.3).
By the cycle identity, z(R^D/ϖ) = Σ_σ m_σ(τ)C_σ(ρ̄); since R^D is O-flat, R^D ≠ 0 iff R^D/ϖ ≠ 0 iff some σ with m_σ(τ) > 0 has C_σ(ρ̄) ≠ 0.

C_σ(ρ̄) ≠ 0 iff σ admits ρ̄: for p ≥ 5, End ρ̄ = k, from Paškūnas 2015 Theorem 1.1(iii) (z(σ, ρ̄) ≠ 0 iff Hom_K(σ, β) ≠ 0) and the K-socle of β; in general this matching of BCDT's explicit list with the cycles is recorded as gap G3.
acceptance: Weight 2, τ trivial (crystalline): admittance by σ_{0,0} ⇔ ρ̄ has a crystalline lift with Hodge–Tate weights 0, 1 (finite flat).

sources.match: Conjectures that, for ρ̄ with centraliser k and types with tamely ramified determinant and non-central image, τ admits ρ̄ iff R^D_{V,O} ≠ 0, and simply admits iff acceptable.

nodes.title: Paškūnas 2015: Breuil–Mézard for p ≥ 5 and End ρ̄ = k
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 5 and ρ̄ : G_{ℚ_p} → GL₂(k) with End_{G_{ℚ_p}}(ρ̄) = k (ρ̄ absolutely irreducible or a non-split extension of two distinct characters), R_ρ̄ its universal deformation ring. For every p-adic Hodge type (w, τ, ψ) in the normalisation of R30.5/breuil-mezard-cycles (det = ψ, ψ|_I = ε^{a+b}det τ): (i) there is a reduced, two-dimensional, O-torsion free quotient R^ψ_ρ̄(w, τ) (resp. R^{ψ,cr}_ρ̄(w, τ)) of R_ρ̄ whose L-points are the potentially semistable (resp. crystalline) deformations of type (w, τ, ψ); (ii) for each irreducible smooth k-representation σ of K there is a one-dimensional cycle z(σ, ρ̄) of R_ρ̄, independent of (w, τ), with z₁(R^ψ_ρ̄(w, τ)/ϖ) = Σ_σ m_σ(w, τ)z(σ, ρ̄) and z₁(R^{ψ,cr}_ρ̄(w, τ)/ϖ) = Σ_σ m^cr_σ(w, τ)z(σ, ρ̄); (iii) z(σ, ρ̄) ≠ 0 iff Hom_K(σ, β) ≠ 0, β the atom attached to ρ̄ by Colmez, and then its Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity is 1, except for ρ̄ ≅ (ω *; 0 1) ⊗ χ with * peu ramifié, where it is 2. The result is new only for ρ̄ ≅ (ω *; 0 1) ⊗ χ; the other cases are Kisin's.
hypotheses: p ≥ 5; End(ρ̄) = k. Split ρ̄ (Hu–Tan) and non-split self-extensions (χ *; 0 χ) are not covered.
proofSteps: Apply Paškūnas's criterion (R30.5/paskunas-cycle-criterion) to N = P̃ with End(P̃) = R^ψ_ρ̄ (R30.5/paskunas-endomorphism-rings, R30.5/dual-of-universal-deformation).
Supports of M(Θ) for Θ ⊂ σ(w, τ): Proposition 4.14 via R30.4/kisin-hypothesis and R30.4/locally-algebraic-vectors.
Cycles z(σ, ρ̄) := z₁(M(σ)), their nonvanishing and multiplicity: Theorem 6.6 and §6 (generic and non-generic cases; Theorem 6.24 for (χω *; 0 χ)).
acceptance: For ρ̄ absolutely irreducible, z(σ, ρ̄) ≠ 0 exactly for the Serre weights σ of ρ̄ (the K-socle of the supersingular π with V(π) ↔ ρ̄).
For (w, τ) = ((0,1), 1) crystalline, R^{ψ,cr}_ρ̄((0,1), 1) is the finite flat deformation ring and its special fibre cycle is z(1, ρ̄).

sources.locator: Theorem 1.1 and the paragraph after it, pp. 2–3
sources.match: For p ≥ 5 and End ρ̄ = k: the reduced two-dimensional O-torsion free quotients R^ψ_ρ̄(w, τ), the cycle identities with z(σ, ρ̄) independent of the type, nonvanishing iff Hom_K(σ, β) ≠ 0 with multiplicity one except multiplicity two for (ω *; 0 1) ⊗ χ peu ramifié; new only for (ω *; 0 1) ⊗ χ, the rest being Kisin's.

nodes.title: Hu–Tan: Breuil–Mézard for split non-scalar ρ̄, p ≥ 5
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 5 and ρ̄ ≅ χ₁ ⊕ χ₂ with χ₁ ≠ χ₂. For every (k, τ, ψ) (Hodge–Tate weights (0, k−1), WD(ρ)|_I = τ, det ρ = ψε, ψ|_I = ε^{k−2}det τ) there are 4-dimensional cycles Z_{n,m} of the framed ring R^□(ρ̄), independent of (k, τ, ψ), with Z(R^{□,ψ}(k, τ, ρ̄)/ϖ) = Σ_{n,m} a_{n,m}(k, τ)Z_{n,m} and Z(R^{□,ψ}_cr(k, τ, ρ̄)/ϖ) = Σ a^cr_{n,m}(k, τ)Z_{n,m}, where a_{n,m}(k, τ) is the multiplicity of σ_{n,m} = Sym^n k² ⊗ det^m in the reduction of Sym^{k−2} ⊗ σ(τ); moreover Z_{n,m} = Z(R^{□,ψ}_cr(n+2, (ω̃^m)^{⊕2}, ρ̄)/ϖ). The generic case χ₁χ₂^{−1} ∉ {1, ω^{±1}} is Remark 5.7; the non-generic case ρ̄ ≅ 1 ⊕ ω (up to twist) is Theorems 5.11–5.12, with explicit cycles in terms of the three minimal primes of the versal ring over J.
hypotheses: p ≥ 5 (standing assumption); ρ̄ split with distinct characters; scalar ρ̄ and non-split self-extensions are not covered.
proofSteps: Work with versal deformation rings and pseudodeformation rings R^{ps} (R30.5/block-pseudodeformation-ring), transferring to framed rings by formal smoothness of framed over versal rings.
Use Paškūnas's E_B ≅ R^{ps,ζ} and the endomorphism rings of the projective envelopes of the two principal series (R30.5/paskunas-endomorphism-rings) with the criterion R30.5/paskunas-cycle-criterion.
Non-generic case: explicit versal rings (Hu–Tan §3) and Theorems 5.11–5.12.

sources.locator: Notation, p. 1 (p ≥ 5); Theorem 1.1 (Kisin), p. 3; Theorem 1.3, p. 4; Remark 5.7, p. 30; Theorems 5.11–5.12, pp. 32–33 (arXiv)
sources.match: For p ≥ 5 and ρ̄ ≅ χ₁ ⊕ χ₂ with χ₁ ≠ χ₂ there are 4-dimensional cycles Z_{n,m} independent of the type with the Breuil–Mézard identities, Z_{n,m} the crystalline special fibre cycle of type (n+2, (ω̃^m)^{⊕2}); the non-generic case 1 ⊕ ω is Theorems 5.11–5.12.

nodes.title: Tung: Breuil–Mézard for every ρ̄ when p > 2
nodes.statement: Let p > 2 and r̄ : G_{ℚ_p} → GL₂(k) any continuous representation. For each smooth irreducible k-representation σ̄ of K there is a 4-dimensional cycle C_σ̄(r̄) of R^{□,ψ}_r̄, independent of (λ, τ), such that for all p-adic Hodge types (λ, τ, ψ) (λ = (a, b), a > b; det r = ψε, ψ|_I = ε^{a+b−1}det τ) Z(R^{□,ψ}_r̄(λ, τ)/ϖ) = Σ m_σ̄(λ, τ)C_σ̄(r̄) and Z(R^{□,ψ,cr}_r̄(λ, τ)/ϖ) = Σ m^cr_σ̄(λ, τ)C_σ̄(r̄). Consequently every irreducible component of R^□_r̄(σ)[1/p] meets the support of the patched module M_∞(σ) (is automorphic). New only for p = 3 and r̄ a twist of an extension of 1 by ω; the proof is global, by patching.
hypotheses: p > 2; r̄ arbitrary. The proof uses a globalisation of r̄ over an imaginary CM field and the patched module M_∞ of Caraiani–Emerton–Gee–Geraghty–Paškūnas–Shin with local-global compatibility: these global inputs are consumed here as a cited theorem and owned by the global patching roadmaps.
proofSteps: Globalise r̄ (Emerton–Gee), patch (CEGGPS) to obtain M_∞ with an arithmetic action, use local–global compatibility to identify its support on each potentially semistable ring (Tung §3).

Show every component of R^□_r̄(σ)[1/p] is automorphic using the blocks at p = 3 (§2, exceptional block computations with Colmez's functor) and the faithfulness/density results of Emerton–Paškūnas (§4).
Deduce the cycle identity from the automorphy of all components (Emerton–Gee, Theorem 5.5.2).
acceptance: For p ≥ 5 this recovers Paškūnas 2015 and Hu–Tan.
Corollary 4.6: every irreducible component of R^□_r̄(σ)[1/p] is automorphic.

sources.locator: Abstract and introduction, pp. 1–3; Conjecture 1.1, p. 3; Theorem 1.2, p. 4; Corollary 4.6, p. 14 (arXiv v4)
sources.match: For p > 2 proves the cycle version of the Breuil–Mézard conjecture for every r̄, new for p = 3 and twists of extensions of 1 by ω, by showing that every component of a potentially semistable deformation ring meets the support of the patched module.
Uses Tung's main theorem to remove Kisin's remaining hypothesis for p = 3, and Hu–Tan for p ≥ 5.

nodes.title: Paškūnas 2016: Breuil–Mézard at p = 2 for generic blocks
nodes.statement: Let p = 2 and ρ̄ with ρ̄^{ss} in a block of type (i) (supersingular) or (ii) (generic reducible). For the unframed (End ρ̄ = k) case there are cycles {C_σ} ⊂ Z₁(R^ψ/ϖ), one per irreducible σ of K, with z₁(R^ψ(w, τ)/ϖ) = Σ m_σ(w, τ)C_σ and z₁(R^{ψ,cr}(w, τ)/ϖ) = Σ m^cr_σ(w, τ)C_σ for all p-adic Hodge types (w, τ) (det = ψε, ψ|_I = ε^{a+b−1}det τ), C_σ ≠ 0 iff Hom_K(σ, π) ≠ 0, then with multiplicity 1; for ρ̄ = χ₁ ⊕ χ₂ split generic, framed cycles {C_{1,σ}, C_{2,σ}} ⊂ Z₄(R^{ψ,□}/ϖ) with z₄(R^{ψ,□}(w, τ)/ϖ) = Σ m_σ(w, τ)(C_{1,σ} + C_{2,σ}) and the crystalline analogue, C_{i,σ} ≠ 0 iff σ occurs in the K-socle of the corresponding principal series. Henniart's types are not unique for p = 2; the multiplicities do not depend on the choice.
hypotheses: p = 2; blocks of types (i) and (ii) only; the remaining case r̄ ≅ (χ *; 0 χ) is R30.6/tung-bm-p-two.
proofSteps: Local: E_B is the fixed-determinant deformation ring (R30.5/paskunas-endomorphism-rings (iii)); verify Paškūnas's criterion (R30.5/paskunas-cycle-criterion), the multiplicity condition by Proposition 2.33 using Dospinescu's argument with det V̌(Π) = ψε and dim Ext¹ = 3 (Corollaries 2.24, 2.26), and the locally algebraic completion input for p = 2 (proof of Proposition 2.33).
Theorem 2.34 for the unframed ring; Theorem 2.37 for split ρ̄ via [Paškūnas 2015, Theorem 7.3, Remark 7.4].
acceptance: For σ in the K-socle of π, C_σ is a multiplicity-one cycle.

sources.locator: §2, pp. 20–21 (p-adic Hodge types and Henniart's types at p = 2); Proposition 2.33, p. 22; Theorem 2.34, p. 23; Theorem 2.37, p. 24 (arXiv v2)
sources.match: Defines the p-adic Hodge types with ψε ≡ det ρ̄ and ψ|_I = ε^{a+b−1}det τ, notes that Henniart's types are not unique for p = 2 while the multiplicities are, and proves the unframed and framed cycle identities with nonvanishing iff σ is in the K-socle and multiplicity one.

nodes.title: Tung: Breuil–Mézard at p = 2 for every r̄
nodes.statement: Let p = 2. For every continuous r̄ : G_{ℚ_2} → GL₂(k) the cycle and numerical Breuil–Mézard conjectures (Tung's Conjectures 5.1.2 and 5.1.3, the cycle identity of R30.5/breuil-mezard-cycles) hold; this is new for r̄ ≅ (χ *; 0 χ). The proof is by patching: if 2 splits completely in a totally real F, the support of M_∞(σ°) ⊗ ℚ₂ meets every irreducible component of R_∞(σ)[1/2] (Theorem 8.0.1). Globally (Theorem A): for p = 2 a two-dimensional odd ρ with distinct Hodge–Tate weights at 2, modular residual representation with non-solvable image, is modular.
hypotheses: p = 2; the global patching inputs are cited, owned by the global roadmaps.
proofSteps: Patching over totally real fields with 2 totally split (Tung §§4–7) and the globalisation lemmas (§4.3).
The local 2-adic blocks and Colmez's functor at p = 2 (R30.5/blocks-classification, R30.5/local-r-equals-t) control the patched module.
Theorem 8.0.1 gives automorphy of all components, hence Corollary 8.0.2.
acceptance: For r̄ ≅ (χ *; 0 χ), the identity holds with the framed cycles of Tung's Conjecture 5.1.3.

sources.locator: Theorems A–C, pp. 2–3; Theorem 8.0.1 and Corollary 8.0.2, p. 38 (arXiv v3)
sources.match: Proves modularity of 2-adic potentially semistable representations with distinct weights and the Breuil–Mézard conjectures for every r̄ at p = 2 (new for (χ *; 0 χ)) by showing every component of R_∞(σ)[1/2] meets the support of the patched module.
Cites Paškūnas 2016 Theorem 1.1 and Tung 2021b Theorem A for the 2-adic modularity lifting input.

nodes.title: Kisin's local multiplicity inequality through Colmez's functor
nodes.statement: Let p be odd and ρ̄ : G_{ℚ_p} → GL₂(𝔽). Assume Kisin's Hypothesis (1.2.6) for the type (k, τ, ψ) (R30.4/kisin-hypothesis). Then e(R^ψ(k, τ, ψ)/π) ≤ μ_Aut(k, τ, ψ) := Σ_{n,m} a_{n,m}(k, τ) μ_{n,m}(ρ̄), where a_{n,m} are the multiplicities of σ_{n,m} in σ̄(k, τ) and μ_{n,m}(ρ̄) are Kisin's explicit non-negative integers (1.1.6), determined by the crystalline conjecture (1.1.5) in weights k ∈ [2, p+1] (one case left undefined there, see B.1 below). The inequality is proved through Colmez's functor: for ρ̄ absolutely irreducible on the pseudo-representation ring (Proposition (1.6.10)) and then for the deformation ring (Corollary (1.7.2)); for non-trivial extensions of ω₂ by ω₁ with ω₁ ≠ ωω₂, Proposition (1.6.15) and Corollary (1.7.2) (unframed ring, End ρ̄ = 𝔽); for sums of two distinct characters Proposition (1.7.8); for ρ̄ with scalar semisimplification Propositions (1.6.18) and (1.7.10); the crystalline variant e(R^{ψ,cr}/π) ≤ μ^cr_Aut is Proposition (1.7.13), with equality and formal smoothness statements for k ≤ p+1 in Corollary (1.7.14). Gee–Kisin, Appendix B, corrects: (B.1) the definition of μ_{n,m}(ρ̄) when ρ̄ ≅ (μ_λ *; 0 μ_λ) ⊗ ω^m with n = p−2 (multiplicity 1 if * is non-trivial; not determined by Kisin when * is trivial); (B.2) the functor of Lemma (1.7.4) needs the condition that G_{ℚ_p} acts on L_A ⊗_A 𝔽 via ω₁.
hypotheses: p odd; Hypothesis (1.2.6) for the type; the corrections of Gee–Kisin Appendix B (B.1–B.2) applied.
proofSteps: Kisin §1.6: the closure Θ(r) of the image of c-Ind_{KZ}^G L_{k,τ} → Π_r for each deformation r of the pseudo-representation (Hypothesis (1.2.6)) gives a module V(U) over the pseudo-representation ring with rank bounded by 2 (Lemma (1.6.6)); the Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity of its specialisation is bounded by the multiplicities of σ_{n,m} computed with V on Π(r, λ, χ) (Kisin §1.5, Lemma (1.5.2)–(1.5.3)).
Kisin §1.7: pass from pseudo-representations to representations (Lemma (1.7.1), Corollary (1.7.2), Propositions (1.7.8), (1.7.10), (1.7.13)).
Apply Gee–Kisin's errata B.1–B.2.
acceptance: When the local inequality is combined with the global inequality of patching, equality e = μ_Aut follows (Kisin (2.3.2)–(2.3.4)); for p ≥ 5 Paškūnas 2015 proves the local equality directly.

sources.locator: §1.1, Conjectures (1.1.3) and (1.1.5) and (1.1.6), pp. 6–7; §1.5–§1.7: Lemma (1.6.6), Propositions (1.6.10), (1.6.15), (1.6.18), Lemma (1.7.1), Corollary (1.7.2), Propositions (1.7.8), (1.7.10), (1.7.13), Corollary (1.7.14), pp. 16–35 of the author's preprint
sources.match: Bounds the Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity of potentially semistable (and crystalline) deformation rings by μ_Aut using lattices from Hypothesis (1.2.6) and Colmez's functor, first on pseudo-representation rings then on deformation rings.

Errata to Kisin's paper: the multiplicity μ_{n,m}(ρ̄) for ρ̄ ≅ (μ_λ *; 0 μ_λ) ⊗ ω^m with n = p−2 is 1 when * is non-trivial and not defined explicitly otherwise; Lemma (1.7.4) needs G_{ℚ_p} to act on L_A ⊗ 𝔽 via ω₁.

nodes.title: Finiteness of the mod p category of GL₂(ℚ_p) (Paškūnas–Tung)
nodes.statement: For every p and every block B: Z_B is noetherian and E_B is a finitely generated Z_B-module; υ makes Z_B and E_B finitely generated over R^{ps,ζε}_{tr ρ̄_B} (R30.5/local-r-equals-t). For N in C(O)_B the following are equivalent: there is a surjection P_B^{⊕n} ↠ N; m(N) is finitely generated over E_B; m(N) is finitely generated over R^{ps}; k ⊗̂_{R^{ps}} N has finite length; the cosocle of N has finite length — and they hold if N is finitely generated over O[[H]] for a compact open H. For x : R^{ps} → L' with T_x not of the form ψ + ψε, Ban^{adm.fl}_{G,ζ}(L')_{B,𝔪_x} is equivalent to finite length modules over the completion of (R^{ps}[[G_{ℚ_p}]]/J) ⊗ L' at 𝔪_x; if T_x = tr ρ with ρ absolutely irreducible, to finite length R^{ζε}_ρ-modules, and every Π' killed by 𝔪_x is a finite sum of copies of the irreducible Π with V̌(Π) ↔ ρ.
hypotheses: All p; B any block.
proofSteps: Theorem 1.3 of Paškūnas–Tung (finite generation over R^{ps}), noetherianity of R^{ps} by Chenevier, hence Theorem 1.1.
Corollary 6.7: the equivalences, from exactness of m and Nakayama over R^{ps}.
Corollary 6.16: Banach representations at a maximal ideal of R^{ps}[1/p], via Paškūnas 2013 Theorem 4.36 and Corollaries 6.10–6.11.
acceptance: For Π absolutely irreducible non-ordinary, Ban^{adm.fl}_{G,ζ}(L)_Π ≅ finite length R^{ζε}_{V(Π)}-modules, for every p.

sources.locator: Theorems 1.1–1.4 and Corollary 1.5, pp. 2–4; Corollary 6.7, p. 26; Corollary 6.16, pp. 30–31
sources.match: Z_B noetherian with E_B finite over it and over R^{ps}; the five equivalent finiteness conditions on N ∈ C(O)_B; the description of finite length Banach representations at maximal ideals of R^{ps}[1/p], in particular deformations of an absolutely irreducible ρ.

nodes.title: Every π in a block occurs in k ⊗_{R^{ps}} S^∨
nodes.statement: Let B be a block with central character ζ and S ∈ Rep^ζ_B G an admissible object with S|_K injective in Rep^ζ_K, and put M := (k ⊗_{R^{ps,ζ}_B} S^∨)^∨. Then M has finite length. If moreover there is x : R^{ps,ζ}_B → ℚ̄_p whose specialised pseudocharacter is the trace of an absolutely irreducible ρ_x with Π_x := S^∨[1/p]/ker(x) ≠ 0, then every π ∈ B is an irreducible subquotient of M. In CDN's application S is the localised space of automorphic forms on a definite quaternion algebra S_{ψ,λ,𝔪} and x exists by a supercuspidal-at-p automorphic form; that global input belongs to CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility R31.
hypotheses: S admissible in Rep^ζ_B G with injective restriction to K; for the occurrence statement, the existence of the point x (a global input in applications).
proofSteps: Finite length: S^∨ is finitely generated over O[[K]] by admissibility, so Paškūnas–Tung Corollary 6.7 gives that k ⊗̂_{R^{ps}} S^∨ has finite length (R30.6/paskunas-tung-finiteness).

Occurrence: if π ∈ B does not occur in M, then Hom_G(P_π, S^∨/𝔪^j_{ps}S^∨) = 0 for all j, hence Hom_G(P_π, S^∨) = 0 since S^∨ = lim S^∨/𝔪^j S^∨, hence Hom_G(P_π, Θ^d) = 0 for every G-stable lattice Θ of Π_x.

Π_x ≅ Π^{⊕d} with Π absolutely irreducible non-ordinary (Paškūnas–Tung Corollary 6.16), and by compatibility of the p-adic and mod p correspondences π occurs in the reduction of a lattice of Π: a contradiction.
acceptance: For B = {π} supersingular the statement reduces to M ≠ 0.

sources.match: For the localised quaternionic automorphic forms S, M = (k_L ⊗_{R^{ps,ζ}_B} S^∨)^∨ has finite length by Paškūnas–Tung Corollary 6.7, and every π ∈ B occurs in it, using projective envelopes, Paškūnas–Tung Corollary 6.16 and a supercuspidal-at-p automorphic point.
The finiteness criterion and the structure of Banach representations killed by 𝔪_x.

nodes.title: Breuil–Strauch through the Drinfeld tower (Dospinescu–Le Bras)
nodes.statement: Let π be a supercuspidal representation of G = GL₂(ℚ_p) with trivial central character, ρ = JL(π) the corresponding representation of D^×, Σ_n the n-th Drinfeld covering of the half-plane Ω, and V(π) the set of absolutely irreducible Π ∈ Ban^{adm}(G) with Π^{lisse} ≅ π. (i) V(π) ≅ Proj(M_dR(π)) through Π ↦ Fil⁰ D_dR(V(Π)), V(Π) ranging over the absolutely irreducible two-dimensional potentially crystalline representations with Hodge–Tate weights 0, 1 and D_pst(V) ≅ M(π) (classical correspondence normalised à la Tate). (ii) For Π ∈ V(π) and n large (ρ trivial on 1 + p^nO_D) there is a topological G-isomorphism, unique up to scalar, (O(Σ_n)^ρ)* ≅ Π^{an}/Π^{lisse}. (iii) There is a canonical (up to scalar) isomorphism of Fréchet G-modules H¹_dR(Σ_n)^ρ ≅ M*_dR ⊗ π* such that for each line ℒ ⊂ M_dR, the inverse image of ℒ^⊥ ⊗ π* in Ω¹(Σ_n)^ρ is (Π^{an}_ℒ)*, and the resulting 0 → O(Σ_n)^ρ → (Π^{an}_ℒ)* → π* → 0 is dual to (ii).
hypotheses: π supercuspidal with trivial central character (extends to π ⊗ Sym^k, DLB Remarque 1.3(a)); n large.
proofSteps: (i): CDP (R30.3/cdp-correspondence) with det V(Π) = χ_cyc and the Colmez–Fontaine theorem; all filtrations are weakly admissible since the Weil representation of M(π) is irreducible (R30.4/completions-of-locally-algebraic).
(ii): independence of Π^{an}/Π^{lisse} from the filtration (Colmez Théorème VI.6.43, R30.4/locally-algebraic-vectors (ii)) combined with the geometry of Σ_n (DLB §§5–11).
(iii): comparison with de Rham cohomology of Σ_n (DLB Théorème 1.4).
acceptance: Π^{an}_ℒ is an extension 0 → π → Π^{an}_ℒ → Π(π, 0) → 0 with Π(π, 0) independent of ℒ.

sources.locator: Définition 1.1, Théorème 1.2, Remarque 1.3, pp. 4–5; Théorème 1.4, p. 6 (arXiv)
sources.match: For supercuspidal π with trivial central character: V(π) ≅ Proj(M_dR(π)) via the Hodge filtration; (O(Σ_n)^ρ)* ≅ Π^{an}/Π^{lisse} for Π ∈ V(π); the de Rham cohomology H¹_dR(Σ_n)^ρ ≅ M*_dR ⊗ π* with (Π^{an}_ℒ)* the inverse image of ℒ^⊥ ⊗ π*.

nodes.title: The local inputs to modularity lifting, case by case
nodes.statement: The local results of this layer consumed by GL2ModularityLifting R32 and by Dieulefait–Pacetti's proof of Serre's conjecture, each with its hypotheses: (1) p ≥ 5, End ρ̄ = k: Paškūnas 2015 Theorem 1.1 (R30.6/paskunas-bm-scalar-endomorphisms), including the compatibility of classical and p-adic local Langlands (Emerton lg Theorem 1.2.1 and Paškūnas 2015 remove Kisin's condition on locally algebraic vectors); (2) p ≥ 5, ρ̄ = χ₁ ⊕ χ₂ with χ₁ ≠ χ₂: Hu–Tan Theorem 1.3 (R30.6/hu-tan-bm-split), removing the remaining hypothesis of Kisin's lifting theorem for p ≥ 5 (Hu–Tan Theorem 1.4); (3) p = 3, every r̄ (new for twists of extensions of 1 by ω): Tung 2021a Theorem 1.2 (R30.6/tung-bm-p-odd), global via patching; (4) p = 2: Paškūnas 2016 Theorem 1.1 with Theorems 2.34, 2.37 for generic blocks (R30.6/paskunas-bm-p-two) and Tung 2021b Theorem A and Corollary 8.0.2 for every r̄ (R30.6/tung-bm-p-two); Kisin's Theorem 0.1 (potentially Barsotti–Tate, k = 2) for p = 2 as cited by Dieulefait–Pacetti; (5) all odd p: Kisin's local inequality with Gee–Kisin's corrections (R30.6/kisin-local-inequality) and Kisin's Hypothesis (1.2.6) (R30.4/kisin-hypothesis). Dieulefait–Pacetti Theorem 1.4 (p odd: odd ρ with ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ(√p*)}} absolutely irreducible, de Rham at p with weights {0, k−1}, k > 1, modular residual) uses (1)–(3) and (5); Theorem 1.5 (p = 2, non-solvable image) uses (4). The block, deformation-ring and locally algebraic inputs are local; their occurrence in global completed cohomology is CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility R31.
hypotheses: Each row carries the hypotheses of its source; no unqualified 'p-adic local Langlands theorem' is asserted.
proofSteps: Read off the case division in Dieulefait–Pacetti's proofs of Theorems 1.4 and 1.5 (p. 4) and match each cited theorem with its node in this layer.
Check that every row's prime and residual hypotheses are those of the node it points to.
acceptance: For p = 3 and r̄ = (ω *; 0 1) ⊗ χ only row (3) applies.
For p = 2 and r̄ = (χ *; 0 χ) only Tung 2021b applies.

sources.locator: Theorems 1.4 and 1.5 with their proofs, p. 4 (arXiv v2)
sources.match: Theorem 1.4 (p odd) incorporates Hu–Tan Theorem 1.4 for p ≥ 5 and Tung's main theorem for p = 3 to remove Kisin's hypotheses, with Emerton and Paškūnas for the local Langlands compatibility; Theorem 1.5 (p = 2) cites Kisin's Theorem 0.1, Paškūnas 2016 Theorem 1.1 and Tung 2021b Theorem A.
The Fontaine–Mazur type consequence that removes the remaining hypothesis of Kisin's lifting theorem for split non-scalar ρ̄ and p ≥ 5.

Fontaine's equivalences Rep_tors G_{ℚ_p} ≅ ΦΓ^et_tors, Rep_{O_L}G_{ℚ_p} ≅ ΦΓ^et(O_E), Rep_L G_{ℚ_p} ≅ ΦΓ^et(E) through the covariant D(V) = (A ⊗ V)^H and V(D) = ((O_L·A) ⊗ D)^{φ=1}, exact, compatible with tensor products and with Tate duals V(Ď) = V̌ = Hom(V, L ⊗ χ) (Colmez 2010, Théorème I.3.1).

Overconvergence D = E ⊗ D† for every étale D over E and the equivalence ΦΓ^et(E†) ≅ ΦΓ^et(R) (slope zero, Kedlaya), with D_rig = R ⊗ D† (Colmez 2010, Remarque 0.4(ii)–(iii)); Kedlaya's slope of R(δ) is v_p(δ(p)).

Compact-open independence for Banach representations of a locally compact p-adic Lie group G (red-team finding RT-AREA-automorphic-1/17): a unitary K-Banach representation of G with a G-stable unit ball is admissible for one compact open subgroup iff for every compact open subgroup, so that admissibility of G(ℚ_p)-representations may be tested on a compact open; together with the existing ND.6/banach-iwasawa-duality this is the general admissible unitary Banach category that R30.2 specialises to GL₂(ℚ_p).

Admissible locally analytic representations of a locally ℚ_p-analytic group G (duals of coadmissible D(H, K)-modules for a compact open H) and, for an admissible unitary Banach representation Π, the subspace Π^{an} of locally analytic vectors: admissible, dense, with Π ↦ Π^{an} exact (Schneider–Teitelbaum, Inventiones 2003, Theorem 7.1).

gaps.title: G1. The supercuspidal case of Π(V)^alg = LL(V) ⊗ Alg(V) has only a global proof
gaps.detail: For V de Rham, potentially crystalline but not crystabelline (π_p(V) supercuspidal), the identification of the smooth factor of Π(V)^alg with LL(D_pst) is proved by Emerton (lg §7.4) by choosing a modular V' with the same Weil–Deligne type and weights (Colmez VI.6.42) and computing in completed cohomology of modular curves with the weight part of Serre's conjecture; CDP footnote 5 and CDN-Kisin Remarque 0.2(v) record that no purely local proof is known to them. The global inputs (completed H¹ of modular curves: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibility R31; Serre weights: ClassicalSerreModularity) lie downstream of R30.6 (R30.6 → R31.4), so citing them would create a stage cycle. This packet states the theorem with the global input named in its proof steps and leaves the dependency open: either a local proof is planned here, or the consumers that need the supercuspidal case carry the global input as an explicit hypothesis.

gaps.title: G2. p = 2 for the trianguline classification
gaps.detail: Colmez's Représentations triangulines assumes p ≠ 2 (§0.1, footnote 1). The rank-one classification R(δ) and the Ext¹ dimension count for p = 2 are expected from Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao (Cohomology of arithmetic families of (φ,Γ)-modules, 2014), which was not read; a source for p = 2 must be fixed before these nodes are used at p = 2.

gaps.title: G3. BCDT's admittance versus nonvanishing of Breuil–Mézard cycles
gaps.detail: Deducing BCDT Conjecture 1.3.1(1) from the cycle identity needs: C_σ(ρ̄) ≠ 0 iff σ admits ρ̄ in BCDT's explicit sense. Paškūnas 2015 Theorem 1.1(iii) gives C_σ ≠ 0 iff Hom_K(σ, β) ≠ 0 for p ≥ 5 and End ρ̄ = k; matching the K-socle of β with BCDT's list (which is phrased for ρ̄ rather than its Cartier dual, BCDT §1.3) and covering the remaining ρ̄ and primes is not done here.

gaps.title: G4. Emerton's normalisation of π_p(V) and of B(V) against Colmez's LL and Π(V)
gaps.detail: The bridge node fixes Colmez's LL(M) against R16.3 and records V(π) = MF(π)(ε). Emerton attaches χ₁ ⊕ χ₂|·|^{−1} to Ind_B^G(χ₁ ⊗ χ₂) (lg pp. 11–13), uses MF and the factor det^{b+1} (Theorem 3.3.22) or det^b (§7.4, see source issue E3); his table MF(Ind_B^G χ₁ ⊗ χ₂) = χ₁ (p. 19) and Colmez's V(B(δ₁, δ₂)) = δ₁ with B(δ₁, δ₂) = Ind_B^G(δ₂ ⊗ δ₁ω^{−1}) are not reconciled here; the induction and weight conventions of Emerton §3 must be read to write the dictionary B(V) ↔ Π(V(ε^{±1})) and π_p(V) ↔ LL(V).
